The WPvivid — Backup, Migration & Staging WordPress plugin before 0.9.140 does not prevent serialized data it cannot safely unserialize from being re-serialized as a PHP object during a site migration, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant a PHP object that WordPress instantiates after an administrator restores a backup onto a different URL.

The Flamix: Bitrix24 and WooCommerce Products Sync WordPress plugin before 1.7.0 does not restrict or validate an unauthenticated file-exchange request, allowing anyone to write a file with an attacker-chosen name, extension and path to a web-served location and thereby execute arbitrary PHP.

The Probono Form Basic WordPress plugin before 1.3.3 does not validate the real type of files uploaded through its public form, trusting the client-declared MIME type instead, which could allow unauthenticated attackers to upload PHP files to a public directory and execute them before they are deleted, on servers that do not honour the Probono Form Basic WordPress plugin before 1.3.3's Apache-only access restriction.

The Essential Real Estate plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 5.3.3 via deserialization of untrusted input in the 'saved_search_check_result' function. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to inject a PHP Object. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable software, which means this vulnerability has no impact unless another plugin or theme containing a POP chain is installed on the site. If a POP chain is present via an additional plugin or theme installed on the target system, it may allow the attacker to perform actions like delete arbitrary files, retrieve sensitive data, or execute code depending on the POP chain present.

In OpenStack Cinder before 29.1.1, by making an os-initialize_connection request with an IQN that includes a path traversal as part of the connector's initiator element, an authenticated user with a 'member' role may create or overwrite files in the volume host filesystem. Only cinder-volume hosts using the LIO iSCSI target driver are affected. This target driver is typically used with the LVM volume driver.

In OpenStack keystonemiddleware before 13.0.3, by supplying a malicious regular expression when creating an application credential (aka AppCred) access_rules entry, an authenticated user may consume resources in the consuming process making a service unresponsive.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT

Force an MMU reset when emulating an INIT even if paging was already
disabled, as the MMU page role includes guest_mode (L2), i.e. an INIT while
L2 is running with CR0.PG=0 will result in KVM running L1 with a stale MMU
context.

Alternatively, the reset could be scoped strictly to paging being enabled
or L2 being active, but SMM is also encoded in the page role.  Even though
it _should_ be impossible for the vCPU to be INIT'd while SMM is active,
there's zero value in not handling SMM.  At that point, the only scenario
where KVM _doesn't_ need to reset the MMU context is on an INIT with the
vCPU running in Real Mode or Unpaged Protect Mode, and while INIT in those
modes is somewhat common, it's far from a hot path and re-initializing the
MMU is not expensive, especially when the role isn't changing (KVM elides
most of the re-configuration in that case).

Note, like the Fixes commit, this bug only affects nested SVM as INIT is an
unconditional intercept on VMX, i.e. it's impossible to emulate INIT while
L2 is active.

Temporarily keep the guest TLB flush when CR0.PG is being cleared even
though it is fully redundant with the flush that is emitted on all INIT
events (KVM itself only does RESET when a vCPU is being created, i.e. when
CR0.PG must be '0').

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: logitech-hidpp: fix race condition when accessing stale stack pointer

The driver uses hidpp->send_receive_buf to point to a stack-allocated
buffer in the synchronous command path (__do_hidpp_send_message_sync).
However, this pointer is not cleared when the function returns.

If an event is processed (e.g. by a different thread) while the
send_mutex is held by a new command, but before that command has
updated send_receive_buf, the handler (hidpp_raw_hidpp_event) will
observe that the mutex is locked and dereference the stale pointer.

This results in an out-of-bounds access on a different thread's kernel
stack (or a NULL pointer dereference on the very first command).

Fix this by:
1. Clearing hidpp->send_receive_buf to NULL before releasing the mutex
   in the synchronous command path.
2. Moving the assignment of the local 'question' and 'answer' pointers
   inside the mutex_is_locked() block in the handler, and adding
   a NULL check before dereferencing.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: us122l: Add missing NULL check in usb_stream_hwdep_mmap()

usb_stream_hwdep_mmap() reads us122l->sk.s and dereferences it without
checking for NULL.  The stream object is released by usb_stream_free(),
which is reached through us122l_stop() both when the device is
disconnected and when us122l_start() fails, and it leaves us122l->sk.s
set to NULL.  The hwdep file stays usable after that, so a later mmap()

	KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000010-0x0000000000000017]
	RIP: 0010:usb_stream_hwdep_mmap+0x107/0x890 sound/usb/usx2y/us122l.c:182

crashes while reading s->read_size, which sits at offset 0x10.

That NULL is an expected state for this field: usb_stream_hwdep_vm_fault(),
usb_stream_hwdep_poll(), usb_stream_hwdep_ioctl(), usb_stream_stop() and
usb_stream_free() all test it before use.  Only the mmap callback misses
the check, so let it return -ENODEV, matching what the other hwdep mapping
in usx2yhwdeppcm.c does when its shared buffer has not been allocated.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: us122l: Fix NULL dereference at hwdep open and release

usb_stream_hwdep_open() and usb_stream_hwdep_release() pass the result of
usb_ifnum_to_if() straight to usb_autopm_get_interface() and
usb_autopm_put_interface(), without checking it for NULL.

usb_ifnum_to_if() returns NULL once the device is gone, since
usb_disable_device() clears udev->actconfig on disconnect.  The hwdep file
can outlive the disconnect: the card is released with
snd_card_free_when_closed(), so a process that keeps the character device
open reaches the driver's release callback after the USB configuration has
been dropped, and interface_to_usbdev() then dereferences the NULL
interface at offsetof(struct device, parent).  The open callback has the
same problem when it races with the disconnect.

Check both lookups and fail the open with -ENODEV; in release, skip the
runtime PM put when the interface is already gone and still run the rest
of the per-file cleanup.  Move the us122l->first bookkeeping after the
checks so that a failed open no longer leaves a stale file pointer behind.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: usx2y: Initialize idle URBs before submitting streams

usb_stream_start() submits the first two capture and playback URBs and
only afterwards assigns sk->idle_inurb, sk->idle_outurb,
sk->completed_inurb and sk->completed_outurb to the remaining two URBs
of each direction.

A transfer can complete as soon as usb_submit_urb() has been called, so
the completion handler i_capture_start() or i_playback_start() may run
before those pointers are set.  While the stream is still being
synchronized (state below usb_stream_sync1), stream_start() then calls
playback_prep_freqn(sk, sk->idle_outurb) with sk->idle_outurb still
NULL, and the packet descriptors are written through that NULL pointer:

  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
  0xdffffc0000000018: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN
  KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x00000000000000c0-0x00000000000000c7]
  RIP: 0010:playback_prep_freqn+0x11c/0x4a0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:33
  Call Trace:
   <IRQ>
   stream_start+0x5dc/0x8d0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:596
   i_capture_start+0x3da/0x710 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:654
   __usb_hcd_giveback_urb+0x238/0x550 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1657
   usb_giveback_urb_bh+0x20b/0x530 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1691
   tasklet_hi_action+0xa/0x20 kernel/softirq.c:994
   handle_softirqs+0x16f/0x440 kernel/softirq.c:645
   </IRQ>

The four URBs referenced by these pointers are allocated long before and
do not depend on any transfer state, so assign them before the submit
loop.  Keeping the assignment inside the retry path also restores a
well-defined URB rotation when the start frame mismatch handling kills
and resubmits the streams.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: hwdep: Serialize DSP load requests

The check of the loaded DSP indices and the call of the driver's
dsp_load callback in snd_hwdep_dsp_load() are not serialized.  A hwdep
file descriptor can be shared among threads, or inherited across fork,
so two SNDRV_HWDEP_IOCTL_DSP_LOAD requests for the same index can both
observe the index as unloaded and enter the driver's callback
concurrently, even though the device itself is opened exclusively.

This breaks the assumption behind hw->dsp_loaded that a firmware index
is loaded only once.  For example, snd-usb-usx2y hits
WARN_ON(usx2y->as04.buffer) in usx2y_async_seq04_init() and may
allocate the US-428 sequence URBs twice.

Serialize the check, the callback invocation and the bookkeeping with a
per-hwdep mutex, so that the second request returns -EBUSY.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: bcd2000: Fix use-after-free of MIDI URBs on file close

bcd2000_disconnect() calls snd_card_disconnect(), which only prevents
new opens, and then frees the MIDI URBs.  A rawmidi file that was
already open can still be closed afterwards, and its close callback,
bcd2000_midi_output_close(), calls usb_kill_urb() on midi_out_urb.

The URB pointers are cleared on disconnect and their accesses are
serialized with midi_lock, but bcd2000_midi_output_close() reads
midi_out_urb without that lock.  The check can therefore pass just
before the pointer is cleared, and usb_kill_urb() then runs on the URB
that has already been freed:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in usb_kill_urb+0x74/0x80
  Read of size 8 at addr ffff8880078e7d40
   usb_kill_urb
   bcd2000_midi_output_close
   close_substream
   rawmidi_release_priv
   snd_rawmidi_release

  Allocated by: usb_alloc_urb <- bcd2000_init_midi <- bcd2000_probe
  Freed by:     usb_free_urb <- bcd2000_midi_free
                <- bcd2000_disconnect

Take the lock in bcd2000_midi_output_close() and reference the URB with
usb_get_urb() before releasing it.  The URB then stays valid until
usb_put_urb() after usb_kill_urb() has returned, even if a disconnect
frees it in the meantime.  usb_kill_urb() itself cannot run under
midi_lock, as the completion handler takes the same lock.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: usx2y: Refuse a retried DSP load after a failure

snd_usx2y_hwdep_dsp_load() sets up the asynchronous sequence URBs and
the interrupt URB when the FPGA firmware image with index 1 is loaded,
and then creates the ALSA devices.  If usx2y_in04_init() or
usx2y_create_alsa_devices() fails, the URBs that were already set up
are left in place.

The core keeps the index unloaded when the callback fails, so user
space may issue the same request again.  The second attempt then enters
usx2y_async_seq04_init() or usx2y_in04_init() with the URBs still
allocated and trips WARN_ON(usx2y->as04.buffer) or
WARN_ON(usx2y->in04_urb).

The URBs cannot be released at this point: the card may already have
registered PCM devices that user space can still open, and the
disconnect handler accesses the URBs without holding the DSP lock.
Mark the chip as hung instead, so that a retried request is refused
with -ENODEV and the assertions keep their meaning.  The URBs are
released by snd_usx2y_card_private_free() when the card is freed.

A failing usx2y_async_seq04_init() still releases its own URBs, so that
path remains retryable.

In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.0.0 to 2.0.22 and 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, the return value of password hash functions for sha512-pbkdf2 and legacy sha512 were not checked. Starting with OpenSSL 4.0, sha512-pbkdf2 hashing will fail when using the FIPS provider for passwords shorter than 8 characters. This has the effect that newly created passwords would match against any other password with fewer than 8 characters.

Issue summary: The QUIC stack queues a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame also for
retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames. This allows a remote malicious
QUIC stack to queue an unlimited number of RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames.

Impact summary: A malicious remote QUIC peer can trigger an out-of-memory
condition causing a Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

Description: The earlier fix for CVE-2026-84784 was not complete. It
failed to ignore retransmissions of the NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame. The QUIC
implementation created and inserted a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame for every
retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame it received and there was no limit
on how many RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames were queued.

This issue allows a malicious remote QUIC stack to trigger an unbounded
allocation of memory and eventually an out-of-memory (OOM) condition.

FIPS impact: no
The FIPS module is not affected as the QUIC implementation is outside the
OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

Issue summary: Calling EVP_EncodeBlock() with an input length close to INT_MAX
may overflow the calculation of the encoded output size and write past the end
of the caller-supplied output buffer.

Impact summary: No path by which an attacker can trigger this has been
identified. An application that passes an input length near INT_MAX to
EVP_EncodeBlock() could suffer a heap buffer overflow, crashing or corrupting
its own memory, but it must itself supply such a length.

CWE: CWE-190: Integer Overflow or Wraparound

Description: EVP_EncodeBlock() base64-encodes a buffer of a caller-supplied
length into an output buffer that the caller allocates. The caller is expected
to reserve 4*((len+2)/3)+1 bytes. For input lengths close to INT_MAX, the
arithmetic that computes the encoded length overflows a signed integer, so the
function writes more data than the documented output size. The result is a
heap buffer overflow in the calling process.

Reaching this requires an application to pass an input length near INT_MAX to
EVP_EncodeBlock(). OpenSSL's TLS, QUIC and CMS implementations never encode
buffers of that size, and the command line tools cannot practically be made to
do so: the limits on reading a proxy password from a file and on bignum sizes
prevent it. An application that accepts an attacker-controlled length and
forwards it to EVP_EncodeBlock() without its own bound check is exposed.

The severity is Low because no attacker-controlled path to the overflow is
known. The caller must already hold a buffer of about two gigabytes before the
defect can be reached.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Issue summary: Verifying a maliciously crafted CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData
message with CRL checking enabled may consume excessive CPU time, growing with
the square of the message size.

Impact summary: An attacker who can submit a CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData message
to an application that verifies it with CRL checking enabled can occupy a CPU
core for seconds to minutes, causing Denial of Service. Applications that
leave CRL checking disabled are not affected.

CWE: CWE-407: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity

Description: With CRL checking enabled, OpenSSL compares each CRL distribution
point of a certificate against the issuing distribution point of every
candidate CRL. For a nameRelativeToCRLIssuer distribution point, the full name
is the CRL issuer name with the relative name appended. Since the change that
deferred this computation, crl_crldp_check() rebuilds that full name for each
candidate CRL and frees it again.

CMS_verify() and PKCS7_verify() take both the distribution points and the
candidate CRLs from the message, and this scoring runs before any signature is
checked. An application is exposed only if it sets X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK on
the store and does not pass CMS_NOCRL or PKCS7_NOCRL; CRL checking is off by
default. In TLS the CRLs come from the local store, so a peer controls only
the distribution point count.

The cost grows with the product of the distribution point count, the CRL count
and the issuer name length, all chosen by the message author; a few hundred
kilobytes can occupy a CPU core for tens of seconds. Verification still fails
as it should, with no crash, no incorrect result and no memory growth.
Requiring CRL checking is what limits the severity.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

The (Simply) Guest Author Name plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the user Biographical Info (description) field in versions up to, and including, 4.42. The plugin unconditionally calls remove_filter('pre_user_description', 'wp_filter_kses') at plugin load (sfly-guest-author.php:17), which strips WordPress core's sanitization of the user description field for users who lack the unfiltered_html capability (Subscribers, Contributors, Authors). This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in their own profile Biographical Info that will execute whenever a user accesses a page rendering that author's description (such as an author archive or a single-post author bio in default WordPress themes like Twenty Seventeen and Twenty Fifteen).

WWBN AVideo from 6.5 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with upload permission to inject script by submitting a javascript: scheme videoLink for embed videos. The unvalidated URL is rendered into an iframe src in videoEmbeded.php and PlayerSkins.php, executing for viewers including administrators and enabling creation of new administrator accounts.

WWBN AVideo from 11.1 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with streaming permission to inject HTML by supplying an unvalidated url parameter to plugin/LiveLinks/play.php. Attackers can embed a --> sequence to escape the HTML comment in liveVideo.php, creating a shareable link that executes JavaScript in any visitor's session.

WWBN AVideo through c3edcc274c389816d434acadac07ee78eaf330c1 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability because the default node socket server relays autoEvalCodeOnHTML without the PHP-only filter. Unauthenticated attackers can obtain an anonymous socket token and send a spoofed MSG_BATCH message to trigger client eval() in administrators' browsers for account takeover.

Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.4 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in ImageTransforms::normalizeTransform() that allows attackers to instantiate arbitrary classes by supplying class:null with a __class key. Attackers can reach the method through Craft Commerce's payments/pay redirect template calling customer.photo.getUrl() with a crafted transform to instantiate classes like yii\rbac\PhpManager and execute PHP.

NocoDB from 2026.07.0 before 2026.10.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows users with Creator role to inject SQL through unescaped backslashes in the DATETIME_FORMAT formula format argument on MySQL-backed bases. Attackers can place a backslash before a quote to terminate the DATE_FORMAT string literal and read any data reachable by the data source's database user, including tables outside the base.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a credential exposure vulnerability in the connection-test endpoint that allows authorized integration users to redirect stored credentials by overriding connection host, port, and user fields. Attackers can point the test at a server they control to capture offline-crackable PostgreSQL md5 or MySQL handshakes and recover the stored database password.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability because select-field option titles are embedded into MySQL or MariaDB enum/set column definitions with only single-quote doubling, leaving backslashes unescaped. A base creator or owner can end an option title with a backslash to escape the literal and append ALTER TABLE clauses, adding, dropping or renaming columns and altering indexes in the connected database.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to inject raw SQL by persisting a crafted formula parsed_tree reused without revalidation. Attackers can bypass the SQLite metadata path guard with an alias to plant the tree, escalating to super administrator or executing OS commands on external PostgreSQL hosts.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute database functions by supplying zero-argument function calls as column default values. Attackers can plant functions like version() or inet_server_addr() in PostgreSQL or MySQL column definitions and read results through record APIs, disclosing server addresses, role names, and engine details.

NocoDB before 2026.07.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in its MySQL and SQLite clients that inserts the column precision value into generated data-definition statements without numeric validation. Authenticated users with the Creator or Owner base role can supply a crafted precision value when creating or updating a column to close the type declaration and execute arbitrary SQL against the base's data source.

Traefik from 2.11.58 before 2.11.61 contains a resource leak vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust resources by sending Authorization headers with NTLM or Negotiate schemes. Attackers can open many short-lived connections that each allocate a dedicated backend transport never released, exhausting memory, file descriptors and backend connections.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an insecure blueprint trust vulnerability that allows publisher accounts to read secrets and execute PHP by planting or selecting attacker-controlled blueprint files. Attackers can abuse the import@ directive, uploaded YAML media named as the page template, or form.flash_folder to leak password hashes and keys or invoke static PHP methods for code execution.

Issue summary: A DANE-enabled TLS client may crash by dereferencing a NULL
pointer when processing an unusual combination of certificate and TLSA
records.

Impact summary: The impact is limited to a client crash (potential Denial
of Service).

CWE: CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference

Description: A DANE-enabled TLS client that supports TLSA records with at
least one of the PKIX-TA(0) or PKIX-EE(1) usages alongside the DANE-TA(2)
usage may crash by dereferencing a NULL pointer if the server claims a trusted
CA's certificate to be its end-entity certificate and has an unusual mix of
associated TLSA records.

DANE SMTP clients should not be affected since only the
DANE-TA(2) and DANE-EE(3) TLSA record usages are specified applicable
in SMTP.  For example, the Postfix MTA is not affected, while the Exim
MTA does not at present use OpenSSL's DANE implementation.

Use of DANE in validation of RFC7250 raw public keys (RPKs) is also
unaffected, as these only use DANE-EE(3) TLSA records.

Only applications that support combining the DANE PKI with a traditional PKI
are potentially affected.  A DANE-enabled browser or similar, that uses
OpenSSL's DANE API could be affected.

FIPS impact: no
The DANE API is outside the FIPS module boundary.

Issue summary: Receiving crafted out-of-sequence DTLS handshake fragments may
cause OpenSSL to allocate a full message-length reassembly buffer for each
buffered message, so a small amount of wire data consumes a large amount of
memory.

Impact summary: A remote attacker can send a few small crafted DTLS handshake
fragments to make a DTLS server or client allocate well over a megabyte of
memory per connection, which may lead to memory exhaustion and Denial of
Service if many connections are made.

CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

Description: DTLS handshake messages can arrive out of order and fragmented,
so OpenSSL buffers fragments of up to ten out-of-sequence messages until
reassembly is possible. When the first fragment of a new message arrives,
OpenSSL allocates a buffer sized to the full message length declared in the
fragment header, plus a reassembly bitmap, instead of storing only the bytes
actually received. The declared length is capped by the maximum certificate
list size, 128KB by default, and that cap applies to every handshake message
type rather than only to Certificate messages.

Only DTLS endpoints reach this code. TLS, QUIC and applications that do not
use DTLS are unaffected. An attacker sends fragments that declare a large
message length but carry almost no data, using up to ten distinct message
sequence numbers.

A single connection can then hold roughly 1.4MB of buffers from about 156
bytes on the wire. Because the number of buffered messages is capped, memory
exhaustion requires many connections or many peers, which is why the severity
is Low.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

CAST Imaging has multiple path traversal vulnerabilities in various endpoints. The application does not properly validate the path parameters, allowing an authenticated attacker to use "../" sequences to escape the intended directory and read arbitrary files.


Critically, by reading "/proc/self/environ", the attacker can obtain environment variables containing sensitive credentials such as Keycloak and PostgreSQL passwords, leading to full server compromise and administrative access.


The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

LMS (Lan Management System) is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution via unrestricted upload of dangerous file types in the service ticket feature of the client panel. The application does not verify the type or name of files attached to service tickets. An authenticated attacker can upload an .htaccess file to bypass the access restrictions on the storage directory, together with a PHP script. Visiting the uploaded PHP file's URL leads to arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the web server.


This issue was fixed in commit 89dd3f7.

LMS (Lan Management System) is vulnerable to privilege escalation in the lmsd daemon. The daemon loads the libraries listed in the LMS database without checking that they come from a trusted location. An attacker with access to the web server process or with write access to the LMS database can register a malicious library and trigger a configuration reload, causing lmsd to load and execute it. Because the example systemd unit does not set a separate user, lmsd runs as root, allowing the attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges.
This issue was fixed in commit 89dd3f7. The lmsd component was removed. For existing installations that use lmsd, the recommended solution is to disable and remove this component.

LMS (Lan Management System) is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in its e-mail-based Helpdesk ticket intake. The mail parser does not reject Apache .htaccess configuration files or PHP-executable files when saving ticket attachments. A remote unauthenticated attacker can e-mail a Helpdesk ticket with such an attachment; in the default configuration, anyone can request the uploaded file's URL which executes attacker-supplied code with the privileges of the web server process. No operator interaction or LMS client session is required.


The issue was fixed in commit d5059b1.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to inject scripts via the cross_sell_group_name parameter in admin/cross_sell_groups.php. Attackers with per-page access to cross-selling groups can store a script payload that executes in other administrators' browsers, including full administrators, when they view the group listing.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to inject scripts via the orders_status_name parameter in admin/orders_status.php. Attackers with per-page order status access can store payloads that execute in other administrators' browsers when the unencoded status name is displayed.

The Trust Payments Gateway for WooCommerce (JavaScript Library) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.8. The vulnerability exists because the `new_customer_account()` function stores the raw return value of `wp_create_user()` — including a `WP_Error` object returned on username collision — into the order's `tp_userid` post meta before the `is_wp_error()` guard is evaluated; the `add_customer_details_to_thankyou_page()` callback subsequently reads that meta and casts it with `(int)`, causing PHP to coerce any object to integer `1`, after which `wp_set_current_user(1)` and `wp_set_auth_cookie(1)` are called unconditionally. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to authenticate as WordPress user ID 1 — the bootstrap site administrator or, on multisite, a network super-admin — by supplying the `new_username` parameter matching any existing login during checkout and visiting the resulting thank-you page. Exploitation requires the Trust Payments gateway to be active and the attacker to complete a paid order on their own account; the ID 1 administrator username is additionally enumerable via standard WordPress user enumeration techniques.

The Toolbox for Asgaros Forum plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the replace_temp_pics function in all versions up to, and including, 1.2.4. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). This vulnerability is only reachable when the site administrator has enabled the Inline Image Upload feature (disabled by default).

The Kirki - Freeform Page Builder, Website Builder & Customizer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Unauthorized Data Access in versions up to, and including, 6.4.1 via the `kirki_post_apis` AJAX action's `get-dynamic-content-batch` and `get-collection-batch` endpoints. This is due to the plugin opening these resolvers behind a site-wide, resource-unbound preview token (`EditorPreview::has_valid_token()`) that is NOT bound to the specific page the administrator intended to share, combined with the absence of any `list_users` or `can_user_read_post()` capability check inside `HelperFunctions::get_user_dynamic_content()` and `Collection::get_collection_batch()` — the equivalent checks ARE present on the plugin's own REST route (`FrontendRESTController::get_item_permissions_check()`). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers holding any valid read-only share link to extract from the entire user table every user's `user_email`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `nickname`, `registered_date`, arbitrary string-valued `user_meta` (including custom keys such as `billing_phone`), and the e-mail address of every approved commenter — information that WordPress itself withholds from anonymous readers (served only in the `edit` context behind `list_users`).

The immonex Kickstart plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 1.19.0 via the 'inx-r-cidata (JSON blob containing 'template' and 'template_folders')' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. This can be used to bypass access controls, obtain sensitive data, or achieve code execution in cases where .php file types can be uploaded and included. The filename-level sanitization that strips dot-slash sequences applies only to the template filename component, not to the attacker-supplied template_folders directory paths, rendering it ineffective against directory traversal via that parameter.
Dell PowerStore SDNAS contains an out-of-bounds memory vulnerability in the NAS NFS service that an unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit to cause a denial of service.
An issue in PHPGurukul Employee Leaves Management System (ELMS) Version 2.1 allows a remote attacker to escalate privileges via the PHP session management mechanism

Rapid7 Metasploit Framework versions prior to 6.5.10 suffer from an Improper Access Control issue in the msfdb database initialisation component whereby a PostgreSQL cluster initialised via msfdb init is configured with trust authentication and a world-accessible Unix domain socket in /tmp, allowing any local user on the same host to authenticate as the passwordless postgres superuser and execute arbitrary operating system commands as the msfdb owner. 


This issue is fixed in version 6.5.10.

Virtual Keyboard plugin for SquirrelMail through 0.9.1 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script by supplying unsanitized input in the passformname parameter. Attackers can craft GET requests to /plugins/vkeyboard/vkeyboard.php with script payloads in passformname to execute code in victims' browsers and steal session cookies. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

ThinkPHP 2.0 through 2.2 and 3.0 Lite mode contains an eval injection vulnerability in the Dispatcher PATH_INFO parsing, which uses preg_replace with the /e modifier and a double-quoted replacement. Unauthenticated attackers can send crafted requests to index.php with a malicious 's' parameter containing PHP expressions to execute arbitrary code on the server. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

openSIS 5.1 before 9.0 contains a local file inclusion vulnerability that allows authenticated users to include arbitrary files through the modname parameter of ajax.php. Attackers can prefix a payload with misc/ and use ../ directory traversal to read sensitive files like /etc/passwd or execute local scripts in the web server context. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

NUUO NVRmini 2 through 3.0.8 contains a file disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read web-root files by passing a filename to the 'css' parameter of css_parser.php. Attackers can retrieve PHP source files confined to the document root, exposing hardcoded credentials and sensitive application logic. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-17.

Tiny Tiny RSS before commit c68ac04 (2019-03-03) contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users through the unvalidated 'return' parameter. Attackers can craft requests to /public.php?op=login with an absolute external URL in 'return', which is placed in the Location header to send victims to attacker-controlled sites. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2026-02-26.

FineCMS versions 5.0.4 before 5.0.11 contain an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the data2 API action handled by list_tag in libraries/Template.php. Attackers can send GET requests to index.php?c=api&m=data2 with a valid auth hash and the param action=sql sql='...' to execute arbitrary SELECT queries and extract database information. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

Gnuboard5 5.0.1 before 5.3.3.3 and 5.4.0.1 before 5.4.0.2 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the arr_ajax_msg parameter. Attackers can craft GET requests to /plugin/sms5/ajax.sms_emoticon.php, where common.php's @extract($_GET) injects the value into the echoed JSON output, executing script in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

Chamilo LMS 1.11.10 before 1.11.16 contains an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the searchOptionsFromTags function through the options parameter of extra_field.ajax.php. Attackers can send POST requests with a malicious JSON options array to inject SQL into the IN clause and extract database information. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

OpenSNS 3.2.1 contains an unauthenticated code injection vulnerability in the shareBox method of ShareController that allows attackers to invoke arbitrary model methods via the query parameter. Attackers can send crafted GET requests to /index.php?s=weibo/Share/shareBox abusing parse_str and ShareModel::getInfo to reach Schedule::runSchedule and execute code through assert. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-14.

Open Journal Systems 2.1.0 before 3.0.0 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users to external domains by abusing the source parameter. Attackers can send GET requests to /index.php/index/user/setLocale/<locale> with a source value beginning with '@', which UserHandler.inc.php appends to the server host, redirecting victims to attacker-controlled sites for phishing. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2024-12-05.

Synway SMG Gateway Management Software builds through 2022-03-15 contain a path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files via the downfile parameter in /down.php. Attackers can send a multipart POST request to /down.php with a traversal path in downfile to retrieve sensitive files like /etc/passwd. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-20.

QiboCMS V7 contains an arbitrary file download vulnerability in inc/job/download.php that allows unauthenticated attackers to read files by supplying a base64-encoded url parameter to /do/job.php?job=download. Attackers can bypass the .php extension check using the Windows 'ph<' wildcard to download sensitive files such as configuration files containing database credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-18.

PMB 7.3.1 before 7.3.15 and 7.4.x before 7.4.5 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script through unescaped POST parameter names. Attackers can send crafted parameter names to opac_css/index.php extended_search, which empr.inc.php and languages.inc.php reflect into hidden form inputs to execute JavaScript. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

Reddit Top RSS through commit 5e38bfd contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the unescaped score GET parameter. Attackers can craft links with a score value that closes the input value attribute in html.php, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

SLiMS Senayan Library Management System 9.4.0 before 9.4.2 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the destination parameter of /index.php?p=member, which is echoed unmodified into the login form action attribute. Unauthenticated attackers can craft a malicious destination value to inject script and hijack PHPSESSID sessions of victims who access the link. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

Tiki Wiki CMS Groupware 12.12 through 12.14, 15.5 before 18.10, 19.0 before 21.9, 22.0 before 24.3, and 25.0 contain a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the objectId parameter of tiki-ajax_services.php. Attackers can send a crafted GET request with the comment controller and list action to execute arbitrary JavaScript and steal session tokens or credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

phpLDAPadmin 1.1.0 before 1.2.5 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the dn parameter of cmd.php?cmd=template_engine. Attackers can supply an unparseable dn value that pretty_print_dn returns unescaped in the 'No such entry' error, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

Azon Dominator releases through 2024-06-03 contain an SQL injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to manipulate database queries through the cid parameter in /fetch_products.php. Attackers can send crafted POST requests with boolean-based or time-based blind payloads to extract sensitive database information. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2024-07-30.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a mail proxy, undisclosed traffic can cause a use-after-free in an nginx worker process. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
A remote unauthenticated attacker may crash an nginx worker process or corrupt its memory, disrupting service. Remote code execution is a potential impact. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When using the listen directive with the ssl parameter in the http block with TLSv1.3 enabled, an attacker can use a specially crafted TLS connection to cause an infinite loop in the NGINX worker process while reading the HTTP request body. As a result, the worker process stops accepting new connections and processing existing connections. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Impact: This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) of NGINX. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to require client certificates ("ssl_verify_client on") in a non-default stream virtual server, a remote attacker could bypass verification of client certificates.

Impact:
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to bypass verification of client certificates. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use the ngx_stream_ssl_module module with dynamic certificate loading and the ngx_stream_proxy_module module with the proxy_protocol v2 directive, an abbreviated SSL handshake can cause a worker process to terminate.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system. This is a data plane vulnerability only; there is no control plane exposure.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Description:
This issue affects NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/3. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can cause a use-after-free condition in the NGINX worker process, leading to a restart. Exploitation also depends on conditions beyond the attacker’s control. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

This issue affects NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/2. When NGINX processes undisclosed traffic, the flow control window can exceed the allowed threshold, potentially resulting in a heap buffer overflow typically followed by an NGINX worker segmentation fault. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or potentially execute code remotely. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use HTTP/2 for client connections and proxy client requests to a backend, a specially crafted request can result in use-after-free in the worker process, if this process is running low on worker_connections. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.




Impact:



This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or may allow a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

This issue occurs when NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a proxy, the proxied server name includes variables, and a Server Side Includes (SSI) or mirror directive sends a subrequest to a location that resolves the same server name. Under these conditions, a specially crafted HTTP request may cause a use-after-free condition in a worker process. An attacker may also be able to execute code if Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) is disabled or the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: 
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or perform remote code execution (RCE)



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Description
When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured with the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module module, a specially crafted ClientHello message from an unauthenticated attacker causes forged values of the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module variables, affecting virtual server selection. In addition, it may also cause a disagreement with a proxied server terminating the SSL/TLS connection without Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.3 support.

Impact
This vulnerability may allow an attacker to forge values of the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module variables and bypass the NGINX systems stream routing segmentation. As a result, the attacker may be able to route the connection to a privileged or internal backend that should be unreachable and gain access to sensitive information. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.






Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

The Masteriyo LMS – LMS Course Builder, Quizzes & Certificates plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in versions up to, and including, 3.5.1 via deserialization of untrusted input in the course importer. The set_post_metas() method  calls maybe_unserialize() on attacker-controlled postmeta string values parsed from the uploaded JSON import file. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary PHP Objects. Exploitation by unauthenticated attackers requires that the site has enable_instructor_registration=true AND enable_guest_checkout=true AND at least one purchasable course exists. Install.php sets enable_instructor_registration=false on fresh installs, so this is a non-default configuration. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with author-level access and above.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use the try_files and alias directives with a map variable, certain combinations of regular expression captures in map and try_files can cause a segmentation fault in an NGINX worker process.

Impact:
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to cause an NGINX worker process to terminate unexpectedly. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

LimeSurvey 6.5.0 before 6.16.11 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users by supplying arbitrary values to the url parameter. Attackers can send crafted GET requests to index.php?r=editorLink, where EditorLinkController concatenates url and route unvalidated, redirecting victims to attacker-controlled sites for phishing. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2026-03-20.

cPanel & WHM 11.134.0.13 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the mpidentity parameter of /mailman/listinfo. Attackers can send crafted requests with a script-context breakout payload in mpidentity to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2026-06-08.

BizPrint (print-google-cloud-print-gcp-woocommerce) before 4.10.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in its Debug\Core component that allows any authenticated user, including the lowest-privilege Subscriber role, to invoke the getPrinters and sendPrintRequest AJAX actions without a nonce or capability check. Attackers can send a crafted admin-ajax.php request with an arbitrary WooCommerce order_id to dispatch print jobs for other customers' orders and disclose printer configuration, exposing cross-customer PII and abusing printer resources.

k8s-mcp-server manages Kubernetes clusters through the Model Context Protocol. Prior to 1.1.0, SERVER_MODE defaults to SSE, with the listener on 0.0.0.0:8080, but main.go creates the SSE server without an authentication option or context function. The GET /sse handler creates a sessionId that is only a correlation value, and the POST /message handler accepts a loadable sessionId without an authorization or Origin check before dispatching tools/call; consequently, any client able to reach the port can enumerate and invoke registered Kubernetes tools without credentials. Read-only mode is disabled by default, leaving write-capable Kubernetes tools available to run with the server's configured cluster privileges. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 missing authorization in the Kubernetes integration allowed project viewers to use stored credentials
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 stored XSS on the Docker Container Info tab was possible

Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2, 11.11.x <= 11.11.1 fail to enforce the configured GitLab group/namespace restriction on the permalink code-preview feature and the {{get_projects}} MCP tool, which allows an authenticated user with a connected GitLab account to retrieve repository file content or project metadata from projects outside the restricted group via a crafted GitLab permalink or MCP tool call. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00750

Linux Mint Update Manager manages software updates on Linux Mint systems. From 5.4.8 until 5.5.4.3, 5.5.9.1, 5.8.8.1, 5.9.8.1, 6.0.9.1, and 6.1.5.1, mint-refresh-cache passes a user-controlled --parent-window-id value directly to the privileged Synaptic process without validating it as an integer. A local user permitted to execute mint-refresh-cache through sudo can inject additional Synaptic command-line options and achieve arbitrary code execution as root. This issue is fixed in versions 5.5.4.3, 5.5.9.1, 5.8.8.1, 5.9.8.1, 6.0.9.1, and 6.1.5.1.

A flaw was found in ansible-core. When a task or its parameters are marked no_log: true, sensitive values passed to a module's warn() or deprecate() calls are not redacted and are printed in cleartext to stdout/stderr in warning and deprecation messages. The 'warnings' and 'deprecations' keys are retained in the PRESERVE allow-list in lib/ansible/_internal/_task.py when the task result is censored, so sensitive parameters bypass masking and can be disclosed in output captured in terminal sessions, CI logs, and any automation wrapping ansible-playbook, even though every task touching the secrets is marked no_log: true.
PHPGurukul Beauty Parlour Management System V 1.1 is vulnerable to Cross Site Scripting (XSS) in admin/search-invoices.php via the searchdata parameter.

PHPGurukul Employee Leaves Management System v2.1 contains an insufficient verification vulnerability in the password recovery functionality in forgot-password.php. The application allows an unauthenticated user to access the password-change workflow by providing a valid employee ID and corresponding email address without requiring an additional out-of-band verification mechanism.

A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Public News Article Rendering Module of PHPGurukul News Portal Project v4.1 allows authenticated attackers with administrative or sub-administrative privileges to inject arbitrary HTML and JavaScript through the postdescription parameter when creating or editing news articles. The application renders the stored post content without proper output encoding in news-details.php, allowing injected JavaScript to execute in the browsers of users who visit the affected article.

A Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in PHPGurukul News Portal Project V4.1. The $currenturl variable in news-details.php is constructed using unencoded REQUEST_URI and HTTP_HOST server variables and echoed directly into the href attributes of social share links. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this by crafting a URL containing HTML metacharacters to break out of the href attribute and execute arbitrary HTML or JavaScript in the context of the victim's browser.

Network-AI from 5.11.0 before 5.17.2 contains a CORS misconfiguration in McpStreamableServer that reflects localhost Origins into Access-Control-Allow-Origin regardless of bind interface. Attackers controlling a localhost-origin page or DNS-rebinding name can read unauthenticated /tools and /health responses, exposing tool catalogs and bridge metadata on non-loopback binds.

Froxlor before 2.3.16 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated customers to read hidden traffic statistics by calling the Traffic.listing API command. Attackers can authenticate to api.php with their API key and secret to retrieve HTTP, FTP, and mail traffic volumes despite the panel.customer_hide_options restriction.

Fleet before 4.92.0 contains an improper authentication vulnerability that allows attackers to reuse case-mutated security tokens because MySQL token columns used case-insensitive collation. Attackers holding a case-normalized invite or email-change token can redirect a victim's email for account takeover or redeem invites with roles up to Global Admin.

Obot from 0.9.0 before 0.27.0 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to execute shell commands by embedding an EOF line in file-type MCP server configuration values. Attackers can terminate the heredoc in the generated init container script to run commands, modify the MCP server files volume, and reach services on Obot's Docker network.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authorization bypass that allows restricted project users to create resources in the unrestricted default project by targeting projects lacking features.* flags. Attackers can create bridge networks with raw.dnsmasq dhcp-script injection to run scripts as root, or custom volumes with block.create_options mkfs arguments to read host files.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows restricted clients to create and access default project resources by exploiting entitlement checks against the requested project. Attackers can create bridge networks with raw.dnsmasq directives to execute code as root on the host, or manipulate inherited resources via the ?project= parameter.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains a configuration injection vulnerability that allows users who can launch instances from controlled images to inject LXC directives by embedding line breaks in OCI config.json values or oci.entrypoint and oci.cwd keys. Attackers can add liblxc hooks or crafted tmpfs lxc.mount.entry fields to run commands as root on the host or bind-mount host paths, even from restricted projects.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 and 2.0.1, main/lp/lp_ajax_save_objectives.php and public/main/lp/lp_ajax_save_objectives.php trust the request uid parameter instead of the authenticated user identity when saving SCORM learning objectives. Any authenticated student can replace uid with another user's identifier and overwrite that user's objectives because the endpoint performs no ownership check. This issue is fixed in versions 1.11.40 and 2.0.1.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 2.0.3, public/main/course_description/course_description_controller.php assigns contentDescription directly from a teacher's request in the Doctrine-based add and edit paths without cross-site scripting sanitization. The stored value is rendered by src/CoreBundle/Resources/views/Course/about.html.twig through description with raw output, and the /course/{id}/about route is publicly accessible. A teacher can store active content that executes when an authenticated or unauthenticated visitor views the course description, enabling session theft, credential phishing, defacement, or actions in an authenticated victim's session. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 and 2.0.3, main/lp/scormItem.class.php and public/main/lp/scormItem.class.php store an attacker-controlled title element from imsmanifest.xml without cross-site scripting sanitization when a teacher imports a SCORM package. The title reaches c_lp_item.title and is rendered by src/CoreBundle/Resources/views/LearnPath/scorm_list.html.twig through item.title with raw output while Twig auto-escaping is disabled; the default configuration does not apply the optional AI-disclosure sanitization path. Enrolled students or administrators who view the learning-path table of contents can execute the stored content in their browser sessions. This issue is fixed in versions 1.11.40 and 2.0.3.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 and 2.0.3, src/Chamilo/CourseBundle/Component/CourseCopy/CourseRestorer.php and src/CourseBundle/Component/CourseCopy/CourseRestorer.php use paths supplied by an imported legacy course backup without consistently confining them to the extraction directory. A course teacher can import a crafted backup containing parent-directory path segments, causing file operations to write attacker-controlled content outside the intended destination, including PHP-executable or automatically loaded locations. This can result in code execution as the PHP process and compromise course data, user data, credentials, and the host. This issue is fixed in versions 1.11.40 and 2.0.3.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 on the 1.11 release line and in 2.0.0, plugin/cleandeletedfiles/src/ajax.php and public/plugin/CleanDeletedFiles/src/ajax.php pass the request path parameter and list parameter directly to unlink without canonicalization, filename validation, or confinement to the plugin's scanned directories. An authenticated administrator can delete arbitrary files writable by the web server; a cross-site request forgery against an administrator session can reach the same operation. Deleting application source, uploaded content, cache, or configuration files can cause data loss and denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40 on the 1.11 release line. No fixed 2.0 release is established as of this review.

The Datadog Agent collects events and metrics from hosts and sends them to Datadog. Prior to datadog-apm-inject 0.66.0, the Datadog Single Step Instrumentation injector stores helper tooling in a predictable host directory. On Linux or Kubernetes systems with SSI enabled and at least one Java service instrumented through SSI, a local unprivileged attacker with shell access to the same host can influence that tooling and execute code with the privileges of the instrumented Java service. Services that use dd-java-agent without SSI and non-Java language runtimes are not affected. This issue is fixed in datadog-apm-inject 0.66.0.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40, main/inc/ajax/user_manager.ajax.php exposes the update_users action without an authorization check and stores attacker-controlled firstname, lastname, and email values without HTML sanitization. An unauthenticated attacker can modify another user's profile fields, and the stored content executes when user_portal.php, the administrative user listing, user information, social profile, course participant list, or message-composer recipient header renders the modified account. Targeting an administrator account can expose administrator-session data or permit actions in that session. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40, main/dropbox/dropbox_functions.inc.php accepts a literal .htaccess filename in the course dropbox and stores it in a directory served by Apache, where the file can alter handler behavior under the required AllowOverride All configuration. Any authenticated course participant can upload .htaccess and then upload a PHP payload disguised as a .gif, resulting in code execution as the web-server user when the dropbox tool is enabled. This can expose or modify the Chamilo installation, course content, and database credentials. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40, main/inc/ajax/record_audio_rtc.ajax.php concatenates the user-controlled audio_dir parameter with the course document root and passes the result to recursive directory creation without path normalization. An authenticated course user can select directory paths outside the intended course storage tree wherever the web-server account has permission to create directories. The resulting filesystem changes can interfere with application layout or support a separate file-write or code-execution chain, although this endpoint alone is not shown to write attacker-selected file content outside the course tree. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40.

ALTCHA PHP is a lightweight PHP library for creating and verifying ALTCHA challenges. From 2.0.0 until 2.0.3, the verifySolution method skips HMAC signature verification when a challenge payload omits the signature field, even when hmacSignatureSecret is configured. An attacker can remove the signature, supply attacker-selected low-difficulty challenge parameters, solve the resulting proof of work, and submit a payload that verifies successfully, bypassing the CAPTCHA control. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.

A flaw was found in ansible-builder. The regular expression used to strip comments from a collection's requirements.txt during introspection is susceptible to super-quadratic backtracking. A requirements file containing a line with a long run of internal whitespace and no comment character causes the comment-stripping routine to consume CPU time proportional to the square of the line length. An attacker who can get a victim to build an execution environment that includes an attacker-supplied collection can cause the ansible-builder build or introspect process to hang, resulting in a denial of service. This issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact.

A flaw was found in the Ansible language server shipped with the vscode-ansible extension. The regular expression used to extract documentation fragments from Ansible module files is susceptible to quadratic-time scanning. A module file containing a crafted documentation string causes the language server to consume excessive CPU while indexing it, freezing the language service in the developer's editor. An attacker who can get a developer to open or index a workspace containing an attacker-supplied collection can cause a denial of service of the editor language features. This issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact.

An Unrestricted File Upload vulnerability in the admin panel of PHPGurukul News Portal Project V4.1 allows authenticated attackers to upload files with arbitrary content by bypassing weak filename extension validation in add-post.php and change-image.php. Although files are renamed with an image extension upon storage, the lack of MIME type and content validation enables content spoofing, storage of malicious markup, and creates a vector for Remote Code Execution (RCE) with server misconfigurations or secondary Local File Inclusion.

A Session Fixation vulnerability exists in the admin login endpoint (/admin/index.php) of PHPGurukul News Portal Project V4.1. The application fails to regenerate the session identifier (PHPSESSID) upon successful authentication. A remote attacker can exploit this by setting a known session ID in the victim's browser prior to login. Once the victim authenticates, the attacker can reuse the fixed session ID to hijack the victim's authenticated session.

LLMKube is a Kubernetes operator for self-hosted large language model inference across heterogeneous hardware. Prior to 0.9.0, the ModelReconciler accepts arbitrary absolute paths and file:// URIs in Model.spec.source without restricting them to approved roots. A namespace user who can create or update Model and InferenceService resources can cause copyLocalModel to open an attacker-selected file in the controller pod or cause a HostPathVolumeSource to mount an attacker-selected node file when modelCache.enabled is enabled, which is the default. The selected file is copied into model storage and can expose controller service-account credentials or other node secrets outside the attacker's namespace. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

Todoist MCP Server provides tools that allow AI agents to access and modify a Todoist account. Prior to 10.3.3, the optional todoist-mcp-http server accepts browser-origin requests to POST /mcp without validating the Host and Origin headers or authenticating the browser caller. A malicious website can use DNS rebinding to reach the loopback listener and invoke MCP tools through StreamableHTTPServerTransport, which uses the server-held Todoist API key. This exposes Todoist account data and permits operations such as task creation, updates, completion, and deletion. The stdio transport is not browser-reachable and is not affected by this attack path. This issue is fixed in version 10.3.3.

A vulnerability was identified in Relaticle up to 3.10.0. This affects the function mapToField of the file packages/ImportWizard/src/Livewire/Steps/MappingStep.php of the component Import Wizard. Such manipulation of the argument Target leads to authorization bypass. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure.

Open OnDemand is an open-source high-performance computing portal. Prior to Open OnDemand 4.1.6 and 4.2.3, and prior to ood-ansible 4.2.1, the portal generator defaults OIDCCryptoPassphrase to SHA1(servername), and the templates/ood_portal.yml.j2 role checks a different variable from the documented passphrase setting. Administrators who set ood_oidc_crypto_passphrase can therefore believe a strong secret is configured while the deployment continues to use an attacker-derivable value. In OIDCSessionType client-cookie deployments, an unauthenticated remote attacker can derive the encryption key and forge a mod_auth_openidc_session cookie for another user, while server-cache deployments permit lower-impact tampering with protected OIDC state and nonce cookies. This issue is fixed in Open OnDemand versions 4.1.6 and 4.2.3 and ood-ansible version 4.2.1.

Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software. Prior to 3.2.4, the application/controllers/Lotw.php import() workflow passes the lotw_download_url configuration value to curl without scheme validation, accepts file:// content, and writes the response to a predictable path under ./uploads/ that can be retrieved through an unauthenticated HTTP request. A standard user can trigger the LotW import, although changing lotw_download_url normally requires installer administrator access, and related vulnerabilities can remove that prerequisite. The same missing status-validation pattern affects the LotW lotw_users fetch helper and per-user download helper. This exposes files readable by the www-data user, including environment data, mounted secrets, and application configuration. This issue is fixed in version 3.2.4.

Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software. Prior to 2.5, the filename parameter accepted by POST /qsl/addQsoToQsl in application/controllers/Qsl.php addQsoToQsl() is stored without rejecting directory separators or relative path components, and POST /qsl/delete reaches application/models/Qsl_model.php deleteQsl(), which passes the planted qsl_images filename to unlink(). A standard authenticated user can associate the malicious filename with the user's own QSO, satisfy the ownership check, escape the per-user QSL image directory, and delete files writable by the PHP worker. Deleting configuration or operational files can cause denial of service, while deleting installer gate files can reopen the unauthenticated installer and enable application identity takeover through attacker-controlled database configuration. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.

Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software. In 3.2.5 and earlier, the Hams of Note feature stores the administrator-supplied hon_url configuration value through application/controllers/Options.php hon_save() and application/models/Update_model.php update_hams_of_note() fetches that URL without restricting the scheme, host, loopback, link-local, or private network destinations. An administrator can cause the Wavelog server to request arbitrary HTTP or HTTPS destinations from its network position and have parsed response content rendered in the administrator interface, providing a read primitive against otherwise unreachable internal HTTP services. The HTTP status requirement prevents file scheme responses from succeeding, so this issue does not provide local file disclosure. No fixed version is available as of this review.

Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software. Prior to 2.5, the callsign parameter accepted by POST /oqrs/search_log in application/controllers/Oqrs.php search_log() reaches application/models/Oqrs_model.php search_log(), where it is concatenated directly into a raw SQL WHERE clause without parameter binding. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use UNION-based SQL injection to read arbitrary application database records, including account data, password hashes, API keys, station credentials, reset tokens, QSO data, and station metadata. Disclosure of password reset tokens can be combined with the forgot_password workflow to take over accounts, including administrator accounts. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.

WPGraphQL Content Blocks is a WordPress plugin that extends WPGraphQL to support querying Gutenberg blocks as data. Prior to 4.8.6, the editorBlocks renderedHtml field in includes/Data/ContentBlocksResolver.php uses resolve_content_blocks() to read a post with get_post() without applying post_password_required(). An unauthenticated caller who knows a supported post identifier can therefore retrieve the complete body of a password-protected published post without a post password, nonce, or valid cookie, exposing paid, member-only, preview, or internal content. This issue is fixed in version 4.8.6.

OwnPay is a self-hosted open-source payment gateway automation platform. In 0.2.0 and earlier, modules/gateways/alipay/AlipayGateway.php fails open when an Alipay callback lacks a signature or the merchant has no configured public key because verify(array $callbackData, array $credentials) falls back to an undefined mode credential that defaults to test mode, while verifyWebhook() returns true unconditionally. An unauthenticated request to POST /webhook/{gateway} can provide a pending order reference and matching amount, pass both verification gates without a valid payment signature, and cause the order and corresponding payment-received ledger entries to be marked completed. No fixed version is available as of this review.

NotrinosERP is an open-source web-based enterprise resource planning system written in PHP and MySQL. From 1.0.0 until 1.1.0, the employee document handler in hrm/manage/employees.php allows an authenticated user with SA_EMPLOYEE permission to submit doc_file through tab_documents() and stores the raw client filename, including an executable extension, under company/0/documents/employees/ without extension, MIME, or content validation. Uploading a PHP file places executable content beneath the web root, where requesting the stored file results in server-side code execution. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0.

MyMangaDB is a self-hosted manga collection manager with automatic metadata, MyAnimeList import, Docker support, and collection statistics. Prior to 2.7.2, the unauthenticated /api/v1/database/export handler in backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/database.py returns a ZIP containing the live SQLite database and the cover-image library. The database includes the users table and hashed_password values, allowing a remote attacker to obtain all application data and conduct offline password attacks without a session or token. This issue is fixed in version 2.7.2.

MyMangaDB is a self-hosted manga collection manager with automatic metadata, MyAnimeList import, Docker support, and collection statistics. Prior to 2.7.2, the unauthenticated /api/v1/images/manga/save handler in backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/image.py accepts a client-controlled filename and joins it to IMAGE_SAVE_PATH without confining the result. Traversal sequences can escape the image directory and overwrite process-writable files, including DATABASE_PATH for the live SQLite database, while the client-supplied image content type does not validate the uploaded bytes. An attacker can replace the database to plant an administrative user and can overwrite other writable files, causing full application compromise and availability loss. This issue is fixed in version 2.7.2.

MyMangaDB is a self-hosted manga collection manager with automatic metadata, MyAnimeList import, Docker support, and collection statistics. Prior to 2.7.2, the unauthenticated /api/v1/database/import handler in backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/database.py accepts a ZIP archive and moves an included database file to DATABASE_PATH while also replacing IMAGE_PATH content. An attacker can supply a database containing an attacker-controlled users table and administrative account, then authenticate as that account; invalid replacement data can also destroy application data or availability. This issue is fixed in version 2.7.2.
OpenVPN 2.4.0 through 2.6.23 and 2.7_alpha1 through 2.7.8 on Windows allows local authenticated users to execute arbitrary code via a privileged service using user-controlled environment variables.

Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, the database password validation used by the MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, and Redis change-password procedures permits backticks, and the procedures interpolate attacker-controlled passwords into Bash command strings. An authenticated user who can update a database password can trigger command substitution before the database command runs, resulting in arbitrary operating-system command execution with the Dokploy process privileges, which are typically root. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

A vulnerability was found in October CMS up to 4.4.6. This affects the function validateExternalImageHost of the file modules/system/classes/resizeimages/ValidatesExternalImages.php of the component Image Resizer. Performing a manipulation of the argument url results in server-side request forgery. The attack may be initiated remotely. The complexity of an attack is rather high. The exploitability is reported as difficult. The exploit has been made public and could be used. Upgrading to version 4.4.7 mitigates this issue. The patch is named f6372867006c03141944e7b57396a726eb02acf0. You should upgrade the affected component.

MISP contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the Galaxy import/sync functionality (captureGalaxy in app/Model/Galaxy.php). The captureGalaxy() method matched an incoming galaxy payload to an existing galaxy by UUID and unconditionally overwrote the matched record, regardless of whether the importing user belonged to the owning organization or whether the galaxy was a system-provided default galaxy. Any authenticated user holding the perm_galaxy_editor role could therefore: (1) demote a default galaxy by setting its default flag to false, (2) reassign the galaxy's org_id and orgc_id to the attacker's organization, effectively taking ownership, and (3) modify other galaxy fields (name, description, distribution, version). Additionally, the role-level permission check (perm_site_admin or perm_galaxy_editor) was executed after the captureOrganisationAndSG() call, meaning organization and sharing-group data was already captured before the authorization decision was made. The vulnerability requires an authenticated user with the perm_galaxy_editor role and the ability to submit a galaxy import payload containing a UUID that matches an existing galaxy.
