The resulting database write and reset-email send take longer than the nonexistent-account path despite the endpoint returning the same response, allowing timing measurements against a production deployment using a synchronous queue and real SMTP transport to disclose valid staff or customer email addresses. The advisory’s local log-mailer test showed no measurable timing difference, so the signal depends on mail configuration and is useful for follow-on phishing or credential stuffing rather than direct account access. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.0.

TastyIgniter is an open-source online ordering, table reservation, and restaurant management system. Prior to 4.2.0, checkResetPasswordCode() in src/Auth/Models/User.php compares a submitted reset code with the stored 42-character token using a normal string comparison, which can return after the first differing byte instead of taking constant time. The password-reset flow exposes this comparison to remote requests, but the endpoint is rate-limited to six requests per minute per IP, and the advisory reports no live exploit or practical token-recovery demonstration. Recovering a high-entropy reset code through the constrained timing signal could permit an unauthorized password reset. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.0.

TastyIgniter is an open-source online ordering, table reservation, and restaurant management system. Prior to 4.4.4, addFromUrl() in src/Flame/Database/Attach/Media.php performs an outbound HTTP request to a caller-supplied URL and stores the response without validating the URL scheme or destination, which could enable server-side request forgery if a reachable feature passes attacker-controlled URLs to the method. The maintainer reports that no shipped first-party feature calls this method and that it is currently unreachable through product functionality, so no current attack path or impact was identified. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.4.

A vulnerability was determined in itsourcecode Airline Reservation System 1.0. This affects an unknown part of the file admin/navbar.php. This manipulation of the argument page causes cross site scripting. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized.

Community Store for Concrete CMS before 2.8.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script via the order email in single_pages/dashboard/store/orders.php. Attackers can place guest orders with quoted email local parts containing markup to execute script in a store manager's session when viewing the order.

rConfig Core 8.0.0 before 8.2.17 and rConfig Pro before 8.4.0 contain a PHP object injection vulnerability in app/Casts/EncryptStringCast.php that unserializes decrypted attributes without class restrictions. Authenticated attackers can store a serialized gadget chain in encrypted fields like device passwords, triggering command execution as the web server user when read via GET /api/devices.

rConfig Core 8.1.0 before 8.2.20 and rConfig Pro before 8.4.0 contain a missing authorization vulnerability in ExportController.php that allows authenticated users to export restricted tables. Attackers can supply excluded table names to export($table), bypassing the EXCLUDED_TABLES deny list, and obtain decrypted passwords, device credentials, and API tokens.

rConfig Core 8.2.19 before 8.2.22 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to bypass the DeviceIpIsValid loopback guard by supplying unresolved hostnames. Attackers can create a device with a hostname resolving to loopback and device_port_override 6379, causing configuration downloads to send Redis inline commands for remote code execution.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.7.1 through 0.8.4, an incomplete IPv6 blocklist in AutoGPT's outbound SSRF protection allows authenticated users to reach local or private network services. Specifically, _is_ip_blocked and BLOCKED_IP_NETWORKS in autogpt_platform/backend/backend/util/request.py fail to reject the IPv6 unspecified address :: (which connects to ::1 on Linux) as well as 6to4, NAT64, Teredo, and deprecated IPv4-compatible IPv6 encodings. An attacker can pass :: directly to blocks/sql_query_block.py or blocks/email_block.py, or point URL-fetching blocks, web fetch, MCP servers, webhooks, or OAuth at a hostname whose AAAA record resolves to ::. On backends run directly on a host, this exposes unauthenticated internal RPC services and databases listening on ::1, though the default Docker Compose and single-container deployments bind internal services to IPv4 only. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

Several plugins for WordPress published by WP connect (Orders Sync to Airtable for WooCommerce, Add-On for Contact Form 7 to Notion, WP Sync for Notion – Notion to WordPress, Add-On for Contact Form 7 to Airtable, Add-on Brevo for Gravity Forms, and Air WP Sync – Airtable to WordPress) contain embedded malicious code (a backdoor) in the versions listed. The affected releases unconditionally load a backdoor module (includes/airwp-online.php) that runs on every request via the 'init' hook and on a half-hourly WP-Cron event, sends site information (site URL, PHP, WordPress and OS versions, and the server user) to a remote command-and-control server at tascredit-pay.com with TLS certificate verification disabled, and executes the PHP code returned by that server via eval(). The module also accepts queued commands that run shell commands, read, write and delete arbitrary files, query arbitrary database tables, dump the users table including password hashes, drop a webshell into the uploads directory, and install persistent hourly code execution. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers in control of the remote server, or able to intercept its traffic, to execute arbitrary code on the server and fully compromise affected sites. All affected plugins have been closed on WordPress.org and no patched versions are available; we strongly recommend uninstalling them and running a complete malware scan.

An externally-controlled format string vulnerability exists in the authenticated upload_wireguard action of settings/vpnupload.cgi in the ADM. The CGI takes an attacker-controlled WireGuard profile name, inserts it into a JSON object, serializes it, and passes the resulting formatted string directly to printf as the format argument without validation or escaping. An authenticated remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending format string specifiers, or leverage variadic read/write primitives within the non-PIE, non-Canary root CGI to potentially achieve arbitrary remote code execution with root privileges.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

Binding to an unrestricted IP address in the netstack SOCKS5 proxy of the NetBird client (client/iface/netstack) in NetBird versions before 0.74.7 allows an unauthenticated attacker on the same network as the client to relay traffic through the client into its NetBird overlay network. When the client runs in netstack mode (NB_USE_NETSTACK_MODE=true), it starts a SOCKS5 proxy, without authentication, that is meant to bridge applications on the local host into the userspace WireGuard stack. The listener was bound to 0.0.0.0 instead of the loopback address, so any host that can reach the proxy port (1080 by default) can connect and reach peers and internal resources with the network position of the affected client. Netstack mode is not enabled by default. The issue is fixed in version 0.74.7, which binds the proxy to 127.0.0.1 by default.

An unauthenticated attacker can send an unsigned SAML single logout request to force users to log out of Grafana Enterprise instances configured for SAML single logout (improper signature verification).

An argument injection vulnerability exists in the settings/vpn.cgi endpoint in the ADM. When processing a WireGuard profile, the internal command parser removes quotes and performs a quote-agnostic scan on arguments without properly sanitizing redirection operators. An authenticated administrator can supply a crafted parameter to cause the execution helper to open and truncate arbitrary files on the filesystem with root privileges, resulting in an arbitrary file truncation and denial-of-service (DoS) condition.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

An improper input validation vulnerability in the OpenVPN client configuration import feature of ADM allows authenticated administrative users to execute arbitrary operating system commands via a crafted .ovpn profile.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

A path traversal vulnerability in the File Explorer share-link folder-listing endpoint allows a remote attacker with a folder-scoped share link to list directory contents outside the shared folder, including other Samba shares readable by the link creator, because path validation occurs before path canonicalization.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

Since the fix for CVE-2025-64500, Request::getPathInfo() strips the script name from the start of the URL. It does so even when the script name is only the start of a longer path segment. With SCRIPT_NAME set to /index.php, a request to /index.phpadmin gets the path info /admin and is routed like /admin. Encoded spellings such as /index%2Ephpadmin or /%69ndex.phpadmin work too. Before that fix, the path info was admin, which no route matched.

Rules enforced by Symfony are not affected: access_control and firewalls read the same path info as the router. Rules enforced in front of PHP are. The nginx configuration of the Symfony documentation and the .htaccess file of symfony/apache-pack make /index.php/admin unreachable, but they pass /index.phpadmin to the front controller. So a location /admin block in nginx, a <Location /admin> section in Apache, or a CDN or WAF rule on /admin can be bypassed.

The script name is now stripped only when it is followed by /, ? or the end of the URL. A request to /index.phpadmin gets the path info /index.phpadmin.

When Request::getBaseUrl() does not find the script name at the start of the request URI, it looks for it further into the path. This supports web servers that rewrite every URL to a front controller in a subdirectory. The base URL then kept everything before the script name, and the client chooses that part. A request URI starting with // or /\ made the base URL start with a host.

With SCRIPT_NAME=/public/index.php, a request for //evil.example/public/index.php/login is routed to /login, with the base URL //evil.example/public/index.php and the base path //evil.example/public. The URLs generated for that page then point to evil.example:
- links built with path() and the actions of forms, so a login form sends the credentials of the user to evil.example;
- redirects to generated URLs, such as the ones of redirectToRoute();
- assets referenced with a relative path through asset(), so the page can load scripts from evil.example.

The attacker has to make a user follow a crafted link, such as https://app.example//evil.example/public/index.php/login. framework.trusted_hosts does not help, since the host of the request is the real one.

Applications are affected when their front controller is in a subdirectory and the web server sends it URIs that do not start with that directory. A .htaccess file at the root of the project that rewrites every URL to public/ does that, for instance.

Applications are also affected when the web server sets SCRIPT_NAME to the path of the request. Some nginx configurations do that when they send every request to the front controller without fastcgi_split_path_info. php -S does it too, with a router script outside the document root. A request for /\evil.example/index.php then gets the base URL /\evil.example/index.php, which browsers read as a link to evil.example.

The configurations recommended in the Symfony documentation are not affected.

Request::getBaseUrl() now returns an empty base URL when the request URI starts with // or /\.

Most methods of Symfony\Component\Filesystem\Path rely on Path::split(), which takes everything before the first :// as the root of a path. It doesn't check that this prefix is a URI scheme, so the .. segments in that prefix are never resolved. PHP sees a scheme only at the start of a string. So /base/../x://../secret.txt is a plain local path to /secret.txt for PHP, while Path::isBasePath('/base', '/base/../x://../secret.txt') returns true. canonicalize(), join(), makeAbsolute() and makeRelative() are affected the same way.

Some applications check a path built from user input with isBasePath() or canonicalize(), and then open it. They can be made to read or write files outside the expected directory.

On Symfony 6.4 and later, the AssetMapper component builds with Path::join() the path of the files that a remote package references from its CSS. A malicious or compromised package can therefore make importmap:require or importmap:install write a file of its choice outside assets/vendor. For example, the CSS url(../../../../../public/x://shell.php) writes public/x:/shell.php.

A prefix is now a scheme only when PHP would look for a stream wrapper with that name. That is two or more letters, digits, +, - or ., followed by :// at the start of the path. Other prefixes are regular path segments, and the .. segments after them are resolved. Real schemes such as phar://, file://, vfs:// or compress.zlib:// keep working.

The fix for CVE-2026-45756 lowers pcre.backtrack_limit to 10000 around each preg_match() call of the match() and search() filter functions. That limit applies to one starting position, not to one call. PCRE resets its counter at every position it tries a match from. So an unanchored pattern that stays just under the limit is paid once per byte of the subject. Each call also starts from a fresh limit, so chaining clauses in one filter multiplies the work.

Two other paths made the cost of a query grow faster than its size, without any regular expression:
- The filter evaluator scanned the whole expression for logical operators once per node. Its cost grew with the square of the number of chained clauses.
- Queries starting with $ inside a filter, like @.x == $.limit or length($.items), were evaluated again for every node the filter visits.

An application that evaluates an attacker-influenced JSONPath expression can therefore still be made to hold a PHP worker. A document of 2 MB and a query of 2.5 KB take 3.5 minutes of CPU.

JsonCrawler::find() now bounds the total regex work of one call, and throws an exception when that budget is exhausted. Filter expressions are parsed once per query, and absolute queries inside filters are evaluated once per query.

Missing Authentication for Critical Function in Apache Texera (incubating).



The Python virtual environment (PVE) management endpoints of a computing unit are not authenticated by the application itself. In the local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments, which place no authenticating gateway in front of the services, these endpoints are reachable without credentials. The Kubernetes deployment gates them at the gateway, so only the Kubernetes deployment provides the full security model described in SECURITY.md.



This issue affects Apache Texera (incubating): from 1.1.0 through 1.2.0.



Users are recommended to use the Kubernetes deployment, which enforces the full security model, and to upgrade to 1.3.0-incubating, which documents that the local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments do not provide the full security model and should only be used by trusted users.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in the computing unit workflow websocket of Apache Texera (incubating) allows an authenticated user to view workflow results, control workflow executions, and run code in a computing unit they have not been granted. In local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments this is possible directly; in Kubernetes deployments it is possible from code running inside another computing unit in the cluster.



This issue affects Apache Texera : from 1.1.0 through 1.2.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0, which fixes the issue. Local JVM and Docker Compose deployments do not provide the full security model and should only be used by trusted users.

Issue summary: A QUIC peer that sends many small out-of-order STREAM fragments
while withholding the first byte of the stream may cause OpenSSL to buffer
a large number of reassembly nodes occupying much larger memory than
the actual data sent.

Impact summary: A remote peer can pin large amounts of memory on a server that
accepts incoming QUIC streams, potentially exhausting memory and causing
Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

Description: QUIC receive flow control limits the highest byte offset a peer
may reach on a stream. It does not limit how many out-of-order fragments the
receiver buffers. OpenSSL allocates a reassembly node for each non-adjacent
STREAM fragment and never caps the count. A peer that opens a stream and sends
many one-byte fragments at increasing offsets, while withholding the first
byte, makes the receiver retain one node per fragment without delivering any
data.

Only applications that accept incoming streams are exposed. With the default
policy, which rejects peer-initiated streams, the stream is torn down before
state accumulates. Because the read side never advances past the missing
prefix, the flow control window never slides and the nodes stay pinned for the
life of the connection.

The per-stream window bounds the highest offset, so the memory one stream can
pin is finite, but it can reach tens of megabytes and, across many streams and
connections, drive memory pressure and Denial of Service. The severity is
limited because the exhaustion is bounded by flow control and requires a
non-default configuration.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

The sandbox checks that a template may call toString() on an object before converting it to a string. It didn't check the input of tests. The PHP callable of a test may convert this input to a string, for example when its parameter is typed as string. PHP then calls toString() on an object without the sandbox checking it first:

{{ obj is upperish }}

Applications are affected when they register such a test and allow it in the sandbox. No built-in test is affected.

The sandbox now checks the input of tests like the input of filters. The built-in tests that never convert their input to a string still skip the check.

Since Twig 3.28.0, the sandbox skips the toString() check of an argument whose PHP parameter can't hold a string, like an int. A spread argument was mapped to a single parameter, although it fills every parameter from its position on. A sandboxed template could therefore call a denied toString() method:

{{ tag(...[1, obj]) }}

Here, the first parameter of tag() is an int, and a later one accepts strings. Applications are affected when they allow such a function, filter or test in the sandbox. No built-in callable is affected.

A spread argument is now checked unless every parameter that it can fill has a safe type.

Fider before 0.40.0 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to sign in as existing users by linking OAuth identities through unverified email matches. Attackers can use a Google account carrying an unverified copy of a victim's email, including a tenant administrator's, to bind their identity via the OAuthToken handler and obtain persistent session access.

Astra WordPress theme before 4.14.0 contains an improper input neutralization vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers with contributor-level privileges to inject unescaped CSS by submitting a crafted overlay-opacity value in the ast-page-background-meta or ast-content-background-meta REST fields. Attackers can store a malicious payload that, when rendered, causes an uncaught TypeError leading to a fatal error and HTTP 500 denial of service on PHP 8.0+, or injects arbitrary CSS into the page's style block on PHP 7.x enabling UI redress and content spoofing.

HortusFox is a self-hosted web application for collaborative plant management. Prior to 6.2, the toggle_boolean_value() handler in app/controller/admin.php passes the name parameter of the /admin/environment/boolean/toggle route in app/config/routes.php to AppModel::updateSingle() in app/models/AppModel.php, which concatenates the parameter into the SQL UPDATE identifier position without validation. An unauthenticated attacker can induce a signed-in administrator to open a crafted link, causing SQL injection that permits expressions and subqueries to read database contents, including an administrator password hash, or modify settings to enable passwordless administrator access. The hash alone does not permit direct login. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.

HortusFox is a self-hosted web application for collaborative plant management. Prior to 6.2, state-changing AdminController routes in app/config/routes.php accept GET requests. The affected AdminController in app/controller/admin.php does not invoke Asatru\Controller\PostValidator to check CSRF tokens. An unauthenticated attacker can induce a signed-in administrator to open a cross-site link, causing privileged actions such as changing environment settings, deleting users or locations, managing API keys, or clearing cached data. In the tested build, a cross-site POST to /admin/user/update can promote a user immediately after login; in default Chromium the POST succeeds within the approximately two-minute Lax+POST grace period but not with an aged cookie, and other browser configurations may permit the POST. Version 6.2 mitigates the documented GET path, but no complete anti-CSRF fix is documented.

Spug 4.0.0 before 4.1.1 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to execute commands by supplying a crafted git URL to the /api/credential/check/ endpoint. Attackers can inject shell metacharacters into the data field passed to git ls-remote with shell=True, executing commands as the Spug service account, which is root in Docker deployments.

Dell Virtual Storage Integrator for VMware vSphere Web Client, versions prior to 10.12.0.0, contains a Use of Hard-coded Credentials vulnerability in ssl_config.properties. An unauthenticated local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to credential exposure.

Dell Virtual Storage Integrator for VMware vSphere Web Client, versions prior to 10.12.0.0, contains an OS Command Injection – confirm single CWE vulnerability in Upgrade Service. A low privileged remote attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to arbitrary command execution.

Dell Virtual Storage Integrator for VMware vSphere Web Client, versions prior to 10.12.0.0, contains a Server-Side Request Forgery SSRF vulnerability in httpRest.js. A low privileged remote attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to unauthorized access to internal services

Joomla Extension - regularlabs.com - PHP code injection via content inserted during article preparation in Sourcerer extension < 18.0.0 - Sourcerer decided whether PHP may run based on the author or last editor of the host article and applied that decision to complete code blocks that other extensions, such as Users Anywhere, inserted into the article while it was prepared. A user able to edit a value rendered by such an extension, for example the display name in their own user profile, could therefore have PHP executed in the context of a trusted article. Sourcerer 18.0.0 authorizes each executable block against its own source; Users Anywhere 3.1.0, ReReplacer 16.4.0 and Snippets 11.2.0 supply the source information needed to keep executing eligible saved content.

A vulnerability was identified in Volans NGFW Next-Generation Firewall r5.1. Impacted is the function exec of the file sslvpn/sslvpn_client.php of the component SSLVPN Client. Such manipulation of the argument img leads to os command injection. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Canvas 7.0.0 before 7.2.11 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated Contributors to inject scripts by exploiting a libxml2 parser differential in PostBody::clean(). Attackers can publish posts with slash-separated event handler attributes rendered unescaped in show.blade.php, hijacking Editor or Admin sessions to escalate their role to Admin.

OpenResty stream-lua-nginx-module before 0.0.20rc4 contains a use-after-free vulnerability that allows remote peers to trigger access to freed memory when a receiveuntil() pattern iterator is garbage-collected while still referenced by the socket. Attackers can interrupt or close the cosocket connection so later reads or socket closure use the stale pattern pointer, crashing or corrupting the nginx worker.

Super Magic PHPSandbox Command Injection Sandbox Escape Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to bypass the sandbox on affected installations of Super Magic. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the PHPSandbox endpoint. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to execute PHP code. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escape the sandbox and execute arbitrary code in the context of the service account. Was ZDI-CAN-28102.

A vulnerability was identified in Backdrop CMS up to 1.35.2. Affected is the function get_argument of the file core/modules/views/plugins/views_plugin_argument_default_php.inc of the component Views Module. Such manipulation leads to incorrect authorization. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The config-import path enforces no 'use PHP for settings' check while the Views PHP-code argument plugin executes eval() without a permission check, confirming the authorization bypass. The vendor explains: "As per our security advisory policy, no security advisory is required when an exploit requires 'advanced permissions'."

The affected element is the function Store/Update of the file modules/User/Http/Controllers/UserController.php of the component User Management. Performing a manipulation results in dynamically-determined object attributes. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The patch is named 3ae60d57ea6840bb33456596ad799b0a39ca94a2. Applying a patch is the recommended action to fix this issue.

A flaw has been found in JaguarJack catch-admin up to 5.4.1. The impacted element is the function store of the file modules/Permissions/Http/Controllers/RolesController.php. Executing a manipulation can lead to dynamically-determined object attributes. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. This patch is called 3ae60d57ea6840bb33456596ad799b0a39ca94a2. It is best practice to apply a patch to resolve this issue.

A flaw was found in Red Hat Enterprise Linux's qemu-kvm virtualization software. A privileged user inside a guest virtual machine could use this flaw to make the host QEMU process copy parts of its own memory into the guest's memory, where the attacker could read it. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to view portions of the host QEMU process memory from within a guest, potentially exposing sensitive information that could aid in further attacks. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to confidentiality.

A vulnerability was identified in nliautaud pico-content-editor up to 02d5ad6c820c5050c542ab9505819b5e0a0ba1af. Affected by this vulnerability is the function Uploads::saveFile/Auth::init of the file src/Uploads.php of the component Authorization Subsystem. Such manipulation of the argument PicoContentEditorUpload leads to unrestricted upload. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. This product operates on a rolling release basis, ensuring continuous delivery. Consequently, there are no version details for either affected or updated releases. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way. This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

A flaw was found in the Keycloak Operator. Deterministic hashes derived from Kubernetes Secrets are published in generated StatefulSet metadata and in KeycloakOIDCClient status. A user with read access to those resources may be able to recover a low-entropy credential referenced by a Secret, even when Kubernetes RBAC denies the user access to the Secret itself.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in generic_ldap_connect in ldap-client-lib.pl that accepts any LDAPS or StartTLS server certificate. Man-in-the-middle attackers can impersonate the LDAP server to capture the bind DN password, often the root DN, and return forged directory data.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in mysql/view_table.cgi that allows MySQL users to inject scripts via unescaped column names. Attackers with CREATE or ALTER privilege can create columns containing HTML payloads that execute in a Webmin administrator's session when the table is viewed.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an insecure download vulnerability in webmin/upgrade.cgi, cluster-webmin/upgrade.cgi and cluster-usermin/upgrade.cgi that fetches upgrade packages over plaintext HTTP with GnuPG signature verification disabled by default. On-path network attackers can substitute a malicious RPM, Debian or tar.gz package during a default upgrade to execute code as root on the Webmin host and managed cluster servers.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a cleartext transmission vulnerability in connect_ldap_db in ldap-server/ldap-server-lib.pl that sends the LDAP root DN password unencrypted when encryption is set to Detect automatically. Passive network attackers observing traffic between Webmin and a remote LDAP server can capture directory root credentials because the connection loop always reaches a plaintext bind attempt.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in postfix/view_mailq.cgi and sendmail/view_mailq.cgi that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script via unsanitized MIME attachment filenames. Attackers can send a message with a crafted Content-Disposition or Content-Type filename that remains queued, executing script in the Webmin session of users viewing it.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in mount/nfs_export.cgi that allows malicious NFS servers to inject scripts through unescaped export paths. Attackers controlling or spoofing an NFS server's mountd replies can return crafted export paths that execute JavaScript in the session of a Webmin user browsing exports.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in mysql/index.cgi that renders MySQL connection error text and server version strings without escaping. Malicious MySQL server operators or on-path attackers on plaintext connections can return markup in error packets or version strings to execute JavaScript in Webmin user sessions.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in init/mass_systemd.cgi that prints unescaped journalctl output when a systemd service fails to start. Attackers can inject script into the journal via logger or sshd invalid user names, executing it in an administrator's Webmin session.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a missing integrity verification vulnerability in usermin/upgrade.cgi that downloads Usermin upgrade packages over plaintext HTTP without signature or digest checks. On-path network attackers or DNS spoofers can supply a malicious RPM, Debian, or tar.gz package whose maintainer scripts or setup.sh execute as root during upgrade.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a header directive injection vulnerability in sendmail/autoreply.pl that allows unauthenticated mail senders to inject autoreply directives by placing them in inbound subject, from, date, or body fields. Attackers can inject Reply-Tracking to delete files at chosen paths, Autoreply-File to exfiltrate files readable by the delivery user, or arbitrary reply headers including To.

The Synoptic Web Designer: best WordPress design tool WordPress plugin through 1.12 does not perform any capability, authentication, or nonce check on an action that is also exposed to unauthenticated visitors, and it builds a database UPDATE statement by concatenating unvalidated request input, allowing unauthenticated attackers to overwrite arbitrary database records, including an administrator's password, and take over the site.
This is only exploitable on PHP 7.x.

The Web To Print Shop : uDraw WordPress plugin through 3.4.0 does not restrict the file paths, extensions or contents written by one of its unauthenticated AJAX actions, allowing unauthenticated users to write arbitrary PHP files to a web-accessible directory and execute code on the server.

The Web To Print Shop : uDraw WordPress plugin through 3.4.0 does not restrict the source URL, destination path or file type when an unauthenticated AJAX action fetches a file and writes it to a web-accessible directory, allowing unauthenticated users to upload executable PHP files and achieve remote code execution, as well as read arbitrary local files.

The fix for CVE-2026-123339 (GHSA-wg5q-m2ww-f3c9) restores the router context of the main request after an inline fragment, but the cause of that issue is still there. A page can render an inline fragment with render() in Twig, or with an ESI tag when no gateway cache is used. While the fragment runs, SubRequestHandler adds 127.0.0.1 to the trusted proxies of every request. Code that reads the main request during that time trusts its X-Forwarded-* and Forwarded headers if the main request came from 127.0.0.1.

Symfony itself reads the main request there:
- asset() takes the base path and the scheme of the main request. With X-Forwarded-Prefix: //evil.example, asset('build/app.js') returns //evil.example/build/app.js, a script loaded from another host. Request::getBasePath() keeps its first result, so when it's first computed inside the fragment, the later asset() calls of the page return such URLs too.
- absolute_url() in Twig, through UrlHelper, takes the host and the scheme of the main request from X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto.

When a shared cache stores the page, every visitor gets these URLs. With asset(), the page then runs scripts from a host chosen by the attacker.

This affects applications reached over HTTP from 127.0.0.1 when that address isn't a trusted proxy. That's the case behind a TLS terminator, a reverse proxy or an HTTP cache running on the same host. When framework.trusted_proxies is not configured, which is the default, every forwarded header is trusted during that window, X-Forwarded-Prefix included. Configuring framework.trusted_hosts doesn't help with asset(), since the prefix is not a host. Applications that get requests directly through php-fpm or mod_php are not affected, and neither are those behind a proxy on another host. REMOTE_ADDR is not 127.0.0.1 there.

SubRequestHandler doesn't change the trusted proxies of every request anymore. Only the requests it builds, and the requests copied from them, trust 127.0.0.1. While a fragment renders, the main request keeps ignoring the forwarded headers sent by the client.

symfony/http-kernel now requires the version of symfony/http-foundation that contains this fix.

Since Symfony 5.4.48, 6.4.16, 7.1.9 and 7.2.0, NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient follows redirects itself, and sends each hop as a new request through the client it decorates. Before a redirect to another origin, it removes the Authorization and Cookie headers it knows about. But the decorated client then added its own default options again. These include the auth_basic, auth_bearer and auth_ntlm credentials, and the Authorization and Cookie headers it was created with. Credentials set with withOptions() on the decorator came back the same way, since the decorator forwards them to the decorated client.

These credentials were then sent to any origin that a response redirected to, for example through an open redirect on the server the application calls. The decorated client alone doesn't send them. The decorator removed the ones passed to request(), but not auth_ntlm. Since Symfony 8.1, DnsResolvingHttpClient follows redirects the same way and is affected too.

With auth_ntlm, curl started the NTLM handshake with the other origin, which could answer with a challenge to get the NTLM response of the application.

On a redirect to another origin, the decorator now passes empty Authorization and Cookie headers and unsets the auth_basic, auth_bearer and auth_ntlm options. The decorated client then can't add its own. Decorators between NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient and the transport, like ScopingHttpClient or CachingHttpClient, can't add theirs either.

The fix for CVE-2026-109449 made the expression parser check the nesting level of long expressions. This check exists since Symfony 5.4.54, 6.4.48, 7.4.21 and 8.1.9. The parser builds a ?: b with the node of a used twice, and the check walked every path to every node. With nested short ternaries, the number of paths doubles at each level, so an expression of 256 bytes never finished parsing.

The expression needs no variable and no function. Any code that parses or lints untrusted expressions is affected, including the ExpressionSyntax validation constraint. evaluate() and compile() parse the expression first, so they hang too.

The nesting check now skips the nodes it already checked, so it takes linear time again. evaluate(), compile() and the messages of runtime errors now use the node of a once, so a is evaluated once, as in PHP.

CsvEncoder::decode() splits each header cell on the key separator, . by default, and nests the decoded rows one level per separator, with no limit. PHP frees nested arrays recursively, so freeing data that is nested deeply enough overflows the C stack and crashes the process. With a stack of 8 MB, a CSV body of 448 KB is enough.

Each row also builds all the levels of its headers again. With a deep header, a CSV body of 2 KB made of short rows allocates more than 128 MB. A body of 1 MB keeps the CPU busy for 10 seconds or more.

Any code that decodes untrusted CSV with the Serializer is affected. From Symfony 7.4.0, this included every #[MapRequestPayload] argument that doesn't restrict acceptFormat, until 7.4.23 and 8.1.11 stopped decoding CSV payloads by default.

CSV headers can now be nested up to 512 levels, the default depth of json_decode(). Decoding also stops when the rows go through more than 16 header levels, or create more than 4 arrays, per byte of data. A header row of up to 5 levels always fits, whatever the rows contain. Beyond these limits, decode() throws a NotEncodableValueException, which #[MapRequestPayload] turns into a 400 response.

Since Symfony 7.4.0, FrameworkBundle chooses the error renderer from the runtime mode of the application, which comes from the APP_RUNTIME_MODE env var. When this variable isn't set, the cli, phpdbg and embed SAPIs default to the CLI mode, and errors are rendered with CliErrorRenderer. This renderer dumps the whole exception, and it did so even when debug was off.

HTTP workers that run under the CLI SAPI and don't set APP_RUNTIME_MODE then sent these dumps as error responses in production. They contain the messages, file paths and traces of the exceptions. Some exceptions reference the request, like the access denied errors of access_control rules. Their dump then contains the server parameters, with all the environment variables of the application.

This affects, for example, the RoadRunner, Swoole and ReactPHP runners of php-runtime, and baldinof/roadrunner-bundle before 3.2.4. The worker mode of FrankenPHP sets the variable and isn't affected.

The CLI renderer is now used only in debug mode.

When the proxy option isn't set, HttpClient takes the proxy from environment variables like http_proxy or HTTP_PROXY. On web servers, it ignores HTTP_PROXY, because PHP puts the Proxy request header there (the httpoxy issue). On the CLI SAPI, it read HTTP_PROXY from $_SERVER, where PHP also puts the environment.

HTTP workers that run under the CLI SAPI put the headers of each request in $_SERVER too. This is the case of spiral/roadrunner-http, which the RoadRunner runner of php-runtime uses, and of baldinof/roadrunner-bundle and php-pm. A client could then send a Proxy header to choose the proxy of the requests that the application sent while handling its request. That proxy received the full requests to http:// URLs, with their credentials, and could forge the responses. For https:// URLs, it learned the host and port through CONNECT.

NativeHttpClient is affected since Symfony 4.3.0, AmpHttpClient since 5.1.0, and CurlHttpClient since 4.4.40, 5.4.7 and 6.0.7.

On the CLI SAPI, HTTP_PROXY is now read from the environment with $_ENV and getenv(), never from $_SERVER. Other SAPIs still ignore it.

Joomla Extension - virtuemart.net - Unauthenticated local file inclusion leading to remote code execution via controller fallback in VirtueMart extension 4.0.0-4.8.7 - The main controller of the component fell back to including a controller file derived from the request without filtering the name, allowing path traversal to arbitrary local PHP files. Depending on the server setup, for example an available pearcmd.php, this could be used to execute code. The issue has been exploited in the wild. Fixed in 4.8.8.

A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability reflected in the usuario[nombre] parameter of the actualizar_cuenta function in the functions.php endpoint. The application does not properly sanitise the received content, meaning that an authenticated user can inject JavaScript code which is reflected in the web interface and in the JSON responses. If another user views the affected content, the code may be executed within the context of their browser.

A vulnerability was determined in dayrui XunRuiCMS up to 4.7.4. The affected element is the function config_add of the file dayrui/App/Cms/Extends/Admin/Category.php of the component Category Handler. This manipulation of the argument list_field causes code injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. It is advisable to upgrade the affected component.

A **NULL pointer dereference** flaw has been found in the acl_check_dns_host_name() and acl_validate_spn_value() functions in source4/dsdb/samdb/ldb_modules/acl.c of the Active Directory domain controller ACL module in the **Samba** package. The checks read the account name after a request that removes it, and they do not test that the value is present. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can update the DNS host name or service principal name of their own computer account can include a removal of sAMAccountName in that same LDAP modify. The directory process crashes. Repeating the modify keeps the directory service unavailable.

A vulnerability was identified in dayrui XunRuiCMS up to 4.7.4. The impacted element is the function down of the file dayrui/Fcms/Library/Api.php of the component Attachment Download API. Such manipulation of the argument ID leads to unrestricted upload. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A race condition during docker cp mount setup in Docker Engine allows a malicious container to leave a read-only bind mount writable while an archive is extracted into the container. When copying files into a container, the daemon bind-mounts the container's volumes into a temporary view and applies the read-only flags afterwards, through a path inside the container's filesystem. A process in the container can change that path in between, so the flags are applied to a different mount and the intended bind mount stays writable for the duration of the copy.

The fix for CVE-2026-61801 added file type and size checks when parsing user and group files in github.com/moby/sys/user, but did not apply them consistently across all parsing and lookup functions. ParsePasswdFile, ParsePasswdFileFilter, GetAdditionalGroupsPath, ParseSubIDFile, ParseSubIDFileFilter, ParseIDMapFile, ParseIDMapFileFilter, LookupUser, LookupUid, LookupGroup and LookupGid could still read large or unbounded files. An attacker who controls the contents of a user or group file processed by an affected application, such as /etc/passwd or /etc/group from a container image, can cause excessive memory or CPU consumption, resulting in a denial of service. Exploitation depends on how the consuming application uses the affected functions. Fixed in v0.5.1 by enforcing the 10 MiB read limit in all affected functions. Docker Engine 29.10.1 includes the fix.

openIMIS before 2026-10 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the OpenSearch reporting dashboard proxy, where the nginx auth_request only verifies login status without checking the declared right before attaching a hardcoded administrative credential to the proxied request, and the backend OpenSearch cluster has its security plugin disabled via a hardcoded compose setting. Any authenticated account, including self-registered or zero-rights users, can exploit this flaw to gain read, write, and delete access to the OpenSearch cluster.

In Eclipse Ditto versions 1.1.0 to 3.9.9, the nginx reverse proxy configurations shipped with Ditto (Helm chart, Docker Compose, Kubernetes and OpenShift deployment files) forward a client-supplied

  `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` header to the Ditto gateway on locations that do not apply nginx authentication, such as `/api/2/connections`. nginx selects the location based on the normalized request URI
  but forwards the raw URI, while the gateway does not treat an encoded slash (`%2f`) as a path separator. A crafted request path is therefore routed by nginx through such an unauthenticated location and
  by the gateway to the regular Things and Policies HTTP API, including routes that send live messages to devices. When pre-authentication is enabled (the default of the Helm chart and the Docker Compose
  setup), an unauthenticated remote attacker can impersonate arbitrary policy subjects and read, modify and delete Things, read Policies, send messages to devices and create entities. Additionally, the
  optional Ingress of the Helm chart (Ditto 3.9.0 to 3.9.9) routes requests directly to the gateway without setting or removing that header, and the WebSocket Ingress of the Helm chart of Ditto 3.3.0 to
  3.8.15 does not set it, allowing the same impersonation without path manipulation when pre-authentication is enabled. This bypasses the fix for CVE-2026-120753.

KubeSphere 4.0.0 through 4.1.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the CertificateSigningRequest controller that allows attackers with permission to create CertificateSigningRequest objects to escalate privileges by exploiting automatic approval of requests carrying a kubesphere.io/username label without verifying the requester's identity or subject match. Attackers can submit a CertificateSigningRequest for the kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client signer with an arbitrary subject such as a platform administrator to obtain a cluster CA-signed client certificate, enabling authentication as the chosen identity and full cluster administrator privilege escalation.

An invalid memory release in the MongoDB PHP Driver extension occurs when certain string-typed options or type-mapping settings are given non-string values. A party who can run PHP code in a process that loads the extension may corrupt process memory. This can lead to reading or changing process memory, running commands as the PHP process user, or crashing the process.

A NULL pointer dereference and invalid memory release in the server discovery component of the MongoDB C Driver may allow an unauthenticated party that controls a server endpoint, or that can alter unencrypted network traffic, to cause a client application to terminate by sending a crafted discovery response.

An incorrect authorization weakness in the embedded relation handling of the Laravel MongoDB library may allow a user with basic application privileges to alter records belonging to other users. After an embedded relation is pre-loaded, a routine write on that record is issued without the constraint that limits it to the record the user is permitted to change. This may result in unintended modification or loss of stored data for other users of the same application.

A query builder component in a MongoDB integration library for a PHP web framework does not run the query-modification callbacks that an application registers with the framework before sending read, update, and delete operations to the database. As a result, a filter that an application relies on to limit which records a request may touch can be omitted silently. A user with basic application privileges may be able to read or change records that the application intended to keep out of reach.

A polymorphic relationship query helper in the MongoDB Eloquent integration for Laravel resolves a record's type identifier inconsistently between the code that stores a relationship link and the code that searches for one. An application that relies on a relationship-absence query to restrict which records a request may see or change can therefore have that restriction silently fail, allowing a user with basic application privileges to read and to modify or remove records the restriction was meant to cover.

A data-query neutralization weakness in the query builder of the MongoDB integration for a PHP web framework allows values supplied to certain bulk counter-update helpers to be interpreted by the database as query expressions rather than stored as plain text. An application that passes externally supplied data into these helpers may write unintended values into stored documents and may result in unintended disclosure of other data held on the same document. No credentials are required of the party supplying the value.

MongoDB C Driver contains an incorrect authorization weakness in the credential-selection logic used by its AWS authentication mechanism. A process-wide credential cache can take precedence over the credentials supplied for an individual connection, so a connection configured with one set of credentials may instead be authenticated under an identity cached earlier in the same process. A party able to cause the application process to open an additional connection may thereby obtain unintended privileges.

An improper handling of repeated fields in encryption key documents in the MongoDB encryption support library may allow memory to be retained without release. A party able to write to the key storage collection, or a database endpoint returning such a document, may cause the memory use of the calling application process to grow for each document parsed, which may reduce performance of that process.

The MongoDB C Driver does not confirm that the party signing a supplied certificate revocation status response is authorized to answer for the certificate being checked. An unauthenticated party that operates the TLS endpoint a client connects to can therefore have a withdrawn certificate accepted. This may result in unintended disclosure of the application's database traffic and in the loss of the revocation decision.

A vulnerability in the MongoDB integration package for the Laravel framework allows an unauthorized user to bypass mass assignment attribute protections. When an application uses attribute deny-lists to guard sensitive model fields, specially crafted request payloads containing database operator keys can circumvent these protections. An unauthorized user with network access to an affected application endpoint can modify guarded attributes, potentially leading to privilege escalation within the application

The MongoDB Rust driver's connection-string parser can include database password text and authentication property values in the error messages it returns when a connection string is malformed. The optional error-redaction feature does not fully remove this text. A party with read access to the application's logs or error output may obtain part or all of a database credential.

A vulnerability was detected in Zhengzhou Weiwei Information Technology mayicms up to 5.8E. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file /box.php?part=member. The manipulation of the argument userid results in sql injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Sandbox protection in Jenkins Pipeline: Groovy Plugin 4403.v471713a_cea_19 and earlier can be circumvented through interface field initializers, allowing attackers with permission to define and run sandboxed Pipelines to bypass the sandbox protection and execute arbitrary code in the context of the Jenkins controller JVM.

Jenkins Script Security Plugin 1436.v1082791135e4 and earlier does not reject @Builder annotations whose builderStrategy member names an arbitrary class when the annotation is referred to using a partially qualified class name, allowing attackers with permission to define and run sandboxed scripts, including Pipelines, to execute code outside the sandbox if a suitable class is present on the classpath of the component that evaluates the script.

Jenkins Gradle Plugin 2.21.1282.v024680ce00a_b_ and earlier does not configure its XML parser to prevent XML external entity (XXE) attacks when processing Maven extension configuration files from build workspaces.

Jenkins Warnings Plugin 13.10251.va_452d3553728 through 13.10365.v85cd7a_c8110b_ (both inclusive) allows defining inline Groovy parsers whose Groovy scripts are compiled on the Jenkins controller without sandbox protection, allowing attackers able to define inline Groovy parsers to execute arbitrary code in the context of the Jenkins controller JVM.

Jenkins Subversion Plugin 1327.vc36e0019a_653 and earlier does not restrict URLs to HTTP or HTTPS schemes in the Sventon repository browser, allowing attackers with Item/Configure permission to determine the existence of paths on the Jenkins controller file system.

Jenkins Subversion Plugin 1327.vc36e0019a_653 and earlier does not restrict URLs to HTTP or HTTPS schemes in the Sventon2 repository browser, allowing attackers with Item/Configure permission to determine the existence of paths on the Jenkins controller file system.

Jenkins Configuration as Code Plugin 2134.ve13a_2fc90835 through 2147.v8a_8d38668c72 (both inclusive), except 2140.2142.v3836c98f1b_30, resolves variables, including references to files on the Jenkins controller file system, environment variables, system properties, and values from configured secret sources, in YAML documents submitted to its configuration validation endpoint, and returns resolved values in error responses, allowing attackers with Overall/SystemRead permission to read arbitrary files on the Jenkins controller file system, environment variables, system properties, and values from configured secret sources.
A cross-site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in Jenkins Nested View Plugin 241.v178f0b_a_cd76a_ and earlier allows attackers to create views.

Jenkins Performance Plugin 1024.ve69e11844523 and earlier does not limit URL schemes for the external report links it creates based on Taurus XML format performance reports, allowing the `javascript:` scheme, resulting in a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exploitable by attackers able to control these reports.
A cross-site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in Jenkins Spira Importer Plugin 4.0.0 and earlier allows attackers to have Jenkins connect to an attacker-specified URL.
A missing permission check in Jenkins Spira Importer Plugin 4.0.0 and earlier allows attackers with Overall/Read permission to have Jenkins connect to an attacker-specified URL.

Jenkins Pipeline DORA Metrics Plugin 40.vdfd2cb_f019d5 and earlier does not correctly perform permission checks in DoraApiAction#doOverview, allowing attackers with Overall/Read permission to view information about jobs they do not have Item/Read permission to.

Jenkins Pipeline DORA Metrics Plugin 40.vdfd2cb_f019d5 and earlier does not correctly perform permission checks in DoraApiAction#doTrends, allowing attackers with Overall/Read permission to view information about jobs they do not have Item/Read permission to.

Jenkins Pipeline DORA Metrics Plugin 40.vdfd2cb_f019d5 and earlier does not correctly perform permission checks in DoraApiAction#doExport, allowing attackers with Overall/Read permission to view information about jobs they do not have Item/Read permission to.

Jenkins Pipeline DORA Metrics Plugin 40.vdfd2cb_f019d5 and earlier does not correctly perform permission checks in DoraDashboardAction#getDeploymentFrequency, allowing attackers with Overall/Read permission to view information about jobs they do not have Item/Read permission to.

Jenkins Pipeline DORA Metrics Plugin 40.vdfd2cb_f019d5 and earlier does not correctly perform permission checks in DoraDashboardAction#getLeadTime, allowing attackers with Overall/Read permission to view information about jobs they do not have Item/Read permission to.

Jenkins Pipeline DORA Metrics Plugin 40.vdfd2cb_f019d5 and earlier does not correctly perform permission checks in DoraDashboardAction#getMttr, allowing attackers with Overall/Read permission to view information about jobs they do not have Item/Read permission to.

Jenkins Pipeline DORA Metrics Plugin 40.vdfd2cb_f019d5 and earlier does not correctly perform permission checks in DoraDashboardAction#getChangeFailureRate, allowing attackers with Overall/Read permission to view information about jobs they do not have Item/Read permission to.

Jenkins Pipeline DORA Metrics Plugin 40.vdfd2cb_f019d5 and earlier does not correctly perform permission checks in DoraDashboardAction#getSlowestStages, allowing attackers with Overall/Read permission to view information about jobs they do not have Item/Read permission to.

Jenkins Pipeline DORA Metrics Plugin 40.vdfd2cb_f019d5 and earlier does not correctly perform permission checks in DoraDashboardAction#getMostFailingStages, allowing attackers with Overall/Read permission to view information about jobs they do not have Item/Read permission to.

Jenkins Rich Text Publisher Plugin 1.5 and earlier does not escape job names in error messages rendered by the Rich Text Portlet, resulting in a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exploitable by attackers with View/Configure permission.

mysql_fdw builds string literals for queries sent to the remote MySQL server with an escaping routine that is not character-set aware. When the connection uses a multi-byte character set such as GBK, SJIS or Big5 and MySQL's default backslash escaping is in effect, a crafted value whose trailing byte is 0x5C absorbs the escaping backslash and leaves the following quote unescaped. The routine handles every pushed-down string constant, including ordinary WHERE-clause literals, so an authenticated user with only SELECT on a foreign table can break out of the literal and run arbitrary SQL on the remote MySQL server with the credentials of the user mapping. The issue is fixed in mysql_fdw 2.10.0. From mysql_fdw 2.10.0, mysql_fdw forces NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES into the session sql_mode and escapes string literals by doubling single quotes.

mysql_fdw accepts several security-sensitive connection options from roles that are not superusers. A role with USAGE on the mysql_fdw foreign data wrapper can set init_command, which runs arbitrary SQL on the remote MySQL server at every connection, including connections made with other users' mappings on a shared foreign server. The same role can set mysql_default_file, ssl_key, ssl_cert, ssl_ca and ssl_capath, which name files read from the PostgreSQL server host, allowing server-side file reads and connection redirection. The issue is fixed in mysql_fdw 2.10.0. From mysql_fdw 2.10.0, only superusers can set init_command, mysql_default_file, ssl_key, ssl_cert, ssl_ca and ssl_capath.

mysql_fdw inserts several values into statements sent to the remote MySQL server without escaping them: the dbname and table_name options in ANALYZE, the remote schema name and the LIMIT TO and EXCEPT table names in IMPORT FOREIGN SCHEMA, and the sql_mode option in the SET sql_mode command. A user who can create or alter foreign tables or foreign servers, or run IMPORT FOREIGN SCHEMA, can break out of the string literal and run arbitrary SQL on the remote MySQL server with the credentials of the user mapping. The issue is fixed in mysql_fdw 2.10.0. From mysql_fdw 2.10.0, mysql_fdw escapes these names and accepts only letters, digits, underscores and commas in sql_mode.

During IMPORT FOREIGN SCHEMA, mysql_fdw copies column metadata returned by the remote MySQL server into the CREATE FOREIGN TABLE statements it runs locally without quoting it. The COLUMN_DEFAULT value is placed directly in the DEFAULT clause, and the name of the generated ENUM type is inserted unquoted. A malicious or compromised MySQL server, or an attacker who can tamper with the connection, can return crafted information_schema metadata and run arbitrary SQL in the local PostgreSQL session of the user who runs IMPORT FOREIGN SCHEMA. The issue is fixed in mysql_fdw 2.10.0. From mysql_fdw 2.10.0, mysql_fdw quotes these values before building the statements.

mongo_fdw builds the mongodb:// connection URI by inserting option values without percent-encoding them, so URI metacharacters (@ : / ? # & =) in a value are parsed as part of the URI structure. A role that is not a superuser but has USAGE on a foreign server can set the username and password options in its own user mapping. An @ or other metacharacter in those values can point the connection at a host the attacker controls, allowing connection redirection, credential capture and man-in-the-middle attacks. Server-level options such as the address, database and replica set can be injected the same way. The issue is fixed in mongo_fdw 5.6.0. From mongo_fdw 5.6.0, mongo_fdw builds the URI with the libmongoc URI API, which encodes credentials, and rejects URI metacharacters in the other option values.

mongo_fdw converts _id values to 12-byte MongoDB ObjectIds with libbson functions that read a fixed number of bytes without checking the input length: 12 bytes for a bytea _id, and 24 characters for name-typed values and $oid fields in JSON. A shorter value causes a read past the end of the input, which can crash the PostgreSQL backend or include adjacent memory in the query sent to MongoDB. Any user who can supply an _id value or predicate on a foreign table can trigger it. The issue is fixed in mongo_fdw 5.6.0. From mongo_fdw 5.6.0, mongo_fdw accepts only valid 24-character hexadecimal ObjectIds and 12-byte bytea values.

An improper certificate revocation check in the MongoDB Python Driver's optional TLS revocation-checking support allows an unauthenticated party that operates the network endpoint a client connects to, and that holds a revoked but still-dated certificate trusted by that client, to have the connection accepted. This may result in unintended disclosure of application credentials and other session data, and in the client treating responses from that endpoint as genuine.

An information exposure weakness in the connection string handling of the MongoDB Ruby Driver can place credential material from the application's own configuration into the text of a parsing error, where an existing redaction control does not apply. A party able to read the application's error output or logs may thereby obtain database credential text together with deployment coordinates. The condition arises entirely within the embedding application process and requires no database authentication.

An out-of-bounds read in the native C BSON decoding extension of the MongoDB Python Driver may allow an unauthenticated party who can supply crafted BSON data to the decoder to cause the application process to terminate. In some configurations, nearby process memory may be included in error messages, which may result in limited unintended disclosure of data.

Nmap before 7.992 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the Comm.ReceivePacket function of the NSE rpc.lua library, which buffers ONC-RPC record fragments using the server-declared fragment length without an upper bound. A malicious RPC service on a scanned host can declare fragments of up to roughly 2.1GB, and up to 400 fragments per call, causing the Nmap process to exhaust memory; the read path is reached by rpcinfo.nse during version detection (-sV) and is shared by the NFS, rusers and NetWorker scripts.

Nmap before 7.992 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the http-cisco-anyconnect.nse script and the anyconnect.lua library, whose redirect handler follows a server-supplied redirect target without checking that it stays on the scanned host. A malicious web server on a scanned host can redirect Nmap to an arbitrary host and port, including internal and loopback addresses the attacker cannot reach directly, making Nmap send a HEAD request followed by a POST request there; response content is not returned to the attacker. The script runs in the default script category (-sC, -A).

Camunda 8.8.0 before 8.8.47, 8.9.0 before 8.9.29, 8.10.0 before 8.10.10, and 8.11.0-alpha1 contain an insecure deserialization vulnerability in the persistent web session feature, which stores session attributes as Java-serialized data in secondary storage and deserializes them via an ObjectInputStream without an ObjectInputFilter. Attackers with write access to the web session index, such as an unauthenticated Elasticsearch cluster deployed via Camunda's docker-compose files, can plant a crafted serialized object and trigger deserialization by presenting a matching session cookie, which combined with a gadget chain like the bundled Commons Collections 3.1-RC1 library can lead to code execution as the Camunda service account.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: limit priority VLAN untag depth

The priority VLAN receive path can repeatedly remove VID 0 tags and retry
packet processing. Unlike the read-only VLAN protocol parser, this path has
no limit on the number of nested tags it consumes.

Each skb_vlan_untag() advances skb->data and resets header offsets. The
offsets are stored in 16-bit fields. With enough nested tags, the network
or transport offset can wrap. A later protocol handler can then derive a
large pull length from the wrapped offsets and access memory outside the
skb allocation.

Apply the existing VLAN_MAX_DEPTH limit to the exceptional VID 0 retry.
Count the tag already stored in skb VLAN metadata as the first level, then
stop before untagging a ninth level. Keep the accounting inside this
uncommon branch so the regular VLAN receive path is unaffected.

A single VID 0 priority tag before a real VLAN tag is valid. No normal
deployment was found that intentionally emits multiple consecutive VID 0
tags; permitting eight levels is therefore conservative.

The issue was found while researching the Linux network receive path for
Google kvmCTF, with OpenAI Codex (gpt-5.6-sol) assisting the analysis. The
affected path, reproducer and fix were manually reviewed and tested.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject mode changes on connected channels

A peer can send a configuration response with an RFC
option for another mode to a connected channel, for
example to switch it from Streaming to ERTM mode.
l2cap_parse_conf_rsp() then changes chan->mode, but
l2cap_ertm_init() is not called again, so the ERTM
sequence lists are never allocated. The next
out-of-sequence I-frame makes l2cap_seq_list_clear()
write through the NULL srej_list.list.

Refuse the channel when a response tries to change
the mode of a connected channel.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject invalid TxWindow in configuration requests

A peer can send an ERTM RFC option with a TxWindow
of zero, which is out of spec. It is stored in
remote_tx_win unchanged and later passed to
l2cap_seq_list_init(), where roundup_pow_of_two(0)
is undefined. On some architectures this results in
a ZERO_SIZE_PTR list and a remote kernel oops.

A TxWindow above 63 is out of spec as well. With
6-bit sequence numbers we would then send more
unacknowledged frames than the sequence space can
tell apart.

Reply with L2CAP_CONF_UNACCEPT and propose the
default TxWindow instead of accepting the value, so
remote_tx_win always stays within 1 to 63. Keep the
parameters of an earlier request then, and do not
treat the request as done because an earlier one was.

Also refuse a zero size in l2cap_seq_list_init(), so
any other path that reaches it with a zero TxWindow
fails the channel instead of the kernel.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: L2CAP: Use default TxWindow for zero socket option

L2CAP_OPTIONS accepts a txwin_size of zero and
stores it in tx_win. The zero is then sent to the
peer in our configuration request, and if the
channel ends up in ERTM mode it is passed to
l2cap_seq_list_init().

Use the default TxWindow instead, as the mode can
still be changed to ERTM during configuration.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vfio/platform: prevent read-only region mappings from becoming writable

vfio_platform_mmap() rejects writable mappings of regions without the
WRITE flag, but leaves VM_MAYWRITE set.  Userspace can map such a region
read-only and then upgrade the mapping to writable with mprotect().

Clear VM_MAYWRITE for regions without the WRITE flag, as i915 does for
its read-only objects and as fixed in drm/vc4 (CVE-2026-68445),
drm/panthor (CVE-2024-53071) and commit a5edadbae57e ("ptp: vmclock:
prevent read-only mappings from becoming writable").

Note this is defensive hardening: no in-tree platform driver currently
publishes a region without the WRITE flag.  The guard costs nothing and
keeps the mmap() interface honest if a read-only region ever appears.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vfio/fsl-mc: prevent read-only region mappings from becoming writable

vfio_fsl_mc_mmap() rejects writable mappings of regions without the
WRITE flag, but leaves VM_MAYWRITE set.  Userspace can map such a region
read-only and then upgrade the mapping to writable with mprotect().

Clear VM_MAYWRITE for regions without the WRITE flag, as i915 does for
its read-only objects and as fixed in drm/vc4 (CVE-2026-68445),
drm/panthor (CVE-2024-53071) and commit a5edadbae57e ("ptp: vmclock:
prevent read-only mappings from becoming writable").

Note this is defensive hardening: the fsl-mc bus publishes all device
regions with the WRITE flag set, so no device can currently reach the
read-only path.  The guard costs nothing and keeps the mmap() interface
honest if a read-only region ever appears.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vfio/cdx: prevent read-only region mappings from becoming writable

vfio_cdx_mmap() rejects writable mappings of regions without the WRITE
flag, but leaves VM_MAYWRITE set.  Userspace can map such a region
read-only and then upgrade the mapping to writable with mprotect(),
writing to MMIO regions the device marks read-only.

Clear VM_MAYWRITE for regions without the WRITE flag, as i915 does for
its read-only objects and as fixed in drm/vc4 (CVE-2026-68445),
drm/panthor (CVE-2024-53071) and commit a5edadbae57e ("ptp: vmclock:
prevent read-only mappings from becoming writable").

Note this is defensive hardening: no in-tree cdx device currently
publishes a region without the WRITE flag.  The guard costs nothing and
keeps the mmap() interface honest if a read-only region ever appears.

Wallos before 5.11.2 contains an infinite loop vulnerability that allows authenticated users or API key holders to exhaust server resources by storing subscriptions with a frequency of 0. Attackers can trigger renew.php or get_monthly_cost.php to loop forever on a P0D interval, pinning PHP workers and hanging the next-payment cron job for all users.

Loginizer before 2.1.4 contains a brute-force lockout bypass vulnerability in loginizer_login_failed() that allows unauthenticated attackers to avoid failed-attempt recording via non-ASCII URL bytes. Attackers can append invalid UTF-8 or 4-byte sequences to wp-login.php or xmlrpc.php request URLs, causing the log INSERT to fail and enabling unlimited password guessing without lockout or email notification.

ProjeQtOr before 13.1.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in tool/getAFieldForAClassById.php that allows authenticated low-privilege users to read any object property. Attackers can request Class=User with an administrator id and field=password or email to retrieve password hashes for offline cracking.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 18.10 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with a fine-grained personal access token to read work items in projects or groups they have access to but that were not granted to the token due to incorrect authorization checks.

metasfresh through 5.175 contains a SQL injection vulnerability in the stressTest_massCacheInvalidation handler of DebugRestController, which concatenates the caller-supplied tableName request parameter into SELECT statements without parameterization or validation and only checks that the caller is authenticated. Authenticated WebUI users with any role can send GET requests to /rest/api/debug/stressTest/massCacheInvalidation with SQL in the tableName parameter to run time-based and error-based blind queries against the PostgreSQL database, extracting sensitive ERP data such as user credentials and financial records while also degrading availability through sleep payloads.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 12.8 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute quick actions through Service Desk emails due to improper input sanitization.

Incorrect authorization in affected versions of network-manager in Ubuntu allows a local attacker with code execution as the whoopsie user to invoke root-restricted D-Bus methods via an Ubuntu-specific D-Bus policy, disrupting network connectivity or altering network configuration.

  An Ubuntu-specific D-Bus policy configuration in NetworkManager granted the whoopsie user unrestricted send access to org.freedesktop.NetworkManager, overriding the default deny-list for root-only methods (SetLogging, Sleep, LoadConnections, and ReloadConnections). A local attacker able to execute code as the whoopsie user could exploit this to disrupt system networking or alter NetworkManager logging and connection configurations.

A vulnerability was determined in WPExperts New User Approve Plugin up to 3.3 on WordPress. Impacted is the function update_user_role of the file includes/end-points/class-users-api.php of the component REST API. Executing a manipulation can lead to missing authorization. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Handesk through 1.5 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in Attachment::storeAttachmentFromRequest() that allows authenticated agents to upload files with arbitrary extensions by attaching them to ticket comments without extension, MIME type, or size validation. Attackers can upload a PHP file via POST /tickets/{ticket}/comments, which is stored under storage/app/public/attachments and served from /storage/attachments/, to achieve remote code execution as the web server user or serve malicious HTML/SVG content from the application origin.

Faveo Helpdesk (Community) through 2.0.3 and 2.0.4.RC.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in ApiExceptAuthController::checkUrl(), reachable through the unauthenticated and unthrottled GET /api/v1/helpdesk/url route, which validates the url parameter only as a well-formed URL, appends the fixed path api/v1/helpdesk/check-url and fetches it with curl with TLS certificate verification disabled and no restriction on the target host, port or address range. Unauthenticated attackers can choose the scheme, host and port of the request to make the server connect to internal hosts and services, including loopback and private addresses, and read the response body, which is returned in the JSON result field.

On Windows, when a connection takes part in a distributed transaction, psqlODBC and its XA library open further connections of their own to finish the transaction. These connections did not keep the security settings of the application's connection:

- When the XA library's first connection attempt failed, it tried again with sslmode=allow, even for a data source configured with sslmode=verify-full or verify-ca.
- The connections the driver opens itself ignored every libpq option given through pqopt, such as channel_binding=require, and the open string it registers with MSDTC carried no pqopt, so the XA library's connections dropped those options too.

An attacker on the network path between the MSDTC host and the PostgreSQL server, without a certificate or credentials, can make those connections go to a server of their choosing without TLS, read and change what they send, and decide the outcome MSDTC records for the transaction.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
