The theme for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'metavalue (via wp-admin/post.php add_meta → post_meta key 'my_field')' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. A Contributor can store a raw script payload in a custom field on their own draft and cause it to execute in an administrator's or editor's authenticated browser session when they preview or publish the post.

The CubeWP Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.32 This is due to the `cubewp_frontend_role_caps()` function, registered on the `user_has_cap` filter, which excludes REST API requests via a `REST_REQUEST` guard but omits a corresponding `XMLRPC_REQUEST` check, causing it to unconditionally widen capabilities for any Subscriber or Contributor on XML-RPC and admin-ajax.php request paths. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Subscriber-level access and above to escalate their privileges to the full Contributor role capability set — gaining `edit_posts`, `delete_posts`, and `read` — allowing them to create, edit, and delete posts through core XML-RPC methods such as `wp.newPost`. Critically, the capability widening is not scoped to CubeWP's own submission handlers but applies globally to all core capability gates on affected request paths, meaning any Subscriber account can exploit this with a single standard XML-RPC call and no CubeWP-specific interaction. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive every capability defined for the Contributor role.

The Download Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.78 via the 'file[page_template]' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. This can be used to bypass access controls, obtain sensitive data, or achieve code execution in cases where .php file types can be uploaded and included. The malicious page_template value is stored when an Author creates or edits a package post, and the inclusion is triggered on any subsequent page view of the package permalink, meaning the include() can be fired by unauthenticated visitors after the payload is planted.

The Advanced Custom Fields: Font Awesome Field plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'acf[field_klzacffa_iconcls] (profile.php) / acf.profile_icon_class (REST)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.2.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is only exploitable when the plugin is configured in FontAwesome 4.x or 5.x compatibility mode and the icon field's return format is set to 'Icon Class', which is the documented usage pattern for rendering icon classes in theme templates.

The Drag and Drop Multiple File Upload for Contact Form 7 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'upload-file' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires that the targeted contact form be configured to accept a non-script extension such as .gpx (or any extension outside the HTML/XML/PHP blocklist), and the uploaded file is served without a Content-Type header, causing browsers to MIME-sniff and execute it as text/html.

The Secure MCP Server for Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor and other AI Agents plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.8 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for attackers (with access to a valid MCP bearer token) to escalate privileges to the token owner's Administrator role — bypassing NHI ability allow-list and scope restrictions entirely — by submitting any valid MCP bearer token (including scope-restricted connection-test tokens) to arbitrary WordPress endpoints such as admin-ajax.php. This requires possession of a valid MCP bearer token, which is routinely issued to any administrator who connects an MCP client to the site. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete Administrator role.

The Newsletters plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to time-based blind SQL Injection via the 'instance[lists]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.18.2 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. The wpmlgetlistfields AJAX handler performs only a nonce check with no capability check, and the required refreshfields nonce is emitted on every wp-admin page including /wp-admin/profile.php, making the endpoint trivially reachable by any authenticated Subscriber.

The MW WP Form plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in all versions up to, and including, 5.1.8 via the 'mw-wp-form_session_mw-wp-form-<FORM_ID>' parameter due to missing validation on a user controlled key. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to overwrite or delete arbitrary WordPress transients in wp_options — including core-managed transients such as wp_styles_for_blocks — enabling injection of attacker-controlled CSS into every front-end page and permanent anchoring of poisoned transient values that never re-expire. The plugin's CSRF check does not prevent exploitation because MW_WP_Form_Data::__construct() registers _save_to_session() on the PHP shutdown hook before the CSRF check runs, causing the transient write to fire even after wp_safe_redirect()+exit; the GET path via the [mwform_formkey] shortcode has no CSRF check at all.

The Everest Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form, Quiz, Survey & Custom Form Builder with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to File Deletion in all versions up to, and including, 3.6.4 This is due to the `delete_entry_files()` function gating file cleanup on a loose `preg_match('/signature_/', $meta_key)` substring check against the entry's meta-key rather than verifying the actual field type, which allows an ordinary Text field whose label begins with "Signature" to generate a qualifying meta-key such as `signature_1` — causing the attacker-controlled value submitted via `everest_forms[form_fields][<field_id>]` to be stored verbatim and later passed to `wp_delete_file()`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete files within the `wp-content/uploads/` directory on the server, as `safe_delete_file()` enforces a realpath boundary that prevents deletion of files outside that directory such as `wp-config.php`. Exploitation requires an administrator to permanently delete the attacker's submitted entry, as the unauthenticated attacker cannot trigger the deletion themselves; the targeted file must also reside within `wp-content/uploads/`. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Nexter Extension – Security, Performance, Code Snippets & Site Toolkit plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the site administrator to have enabled the plugin's SEO module (available via a persistent admin notice), after which the nofollow_comments option is on by default; with comments open, a single unauthenticated POST to wp-comments-post.php is sufficient to plant the payload.

A security flaw has been discovered in nirix Traq 3.9.0-beta.1. Affected by this issue is the function createSession of the file src/Traq/Controllers/UserController.php of the component Login Handler. Performing a manipulation of the argument redirect results in open redirect. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was determined in SourceCodester Online Food Ordering System 1.0. This affects an unknown function of the file /admin/update_food.php. Executing a manipulation of the argument price can lead to sql injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized.

Iceburg CRM through 5.0.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to view server configuration through public/v.php calling phpinfo(). Attackers can request v.php directly, bypassing Laravel routing, to obtain PHP version, extensions, INI settings, DOCUMENT_ROOT, and environment variables.

KodeRover Zadig before 5.1.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in aslan environment kube.go handlers that allows authenticated users to query Kubernetes clusters of other projects. Attackers can supply arbitrary clusterID and namespace values to /api/aslan/environment/kube/ routes to enumerate namespaces, nodes, deployments, workloads, canary mappings, and resource names.

Iceburg CRM through 5.0.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the related_fields and related_field_name routes in routes/data.php that lets authenticated users read restricted module data. Attackers can enumerate field_id values to query related module tables without Permission::checkPermission checks, reading id and name pairs such as user names from ice_users.

The Product Input Fields for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 2.1.0 via the process_file_input_field function. This is due to missing file type validation in the process_file_input_field function, which accepts the client-supplied multipart Content-Type header as the sole type gate and writes the uploaded file to the unprotected pif_temp directory using the verbatim client-supplied filename. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. Exploitation requires that an administrator has configured at least one product with a File-type Product Input Field with the "Show thumbnail" option enabled, which is a standard use of the feature; additionally, the pif_temp/ upload directory is created without .htaccess or index.php restrictions, leaving written files directly web-accessible and executable on default Apache/mod_php configurations.

The WP Statistics – Simple, privacy-friendly Google Analytics alternative plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 14.16.19 via the 'tab' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. This can be used to bypass access controls, obtain sensitive data, or achieve code execution in cases where .php file types can be uploaded and included. The exploitability of this vulnerability depends on the Minimum Role to View Statistics setting; when set to a low-privilege role such as Subscriber (read capability), unauthenticated-equivalent access is effectively granted to any registered user, while the default Administrator setting limits exposure to higher-privileged accounts.

The Simple Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in versions up to, and including, 4.8.9 This is due to the site-wide signing secret `swpm_private_key_one` being generated at install time with PHP's non-cryptographic `uniqid('', true)` function in `SwpmInstallation::installer()`, whose timestamp-derived keyspace (~10^15 candidates / ~50 bits) can be constrained via the public WordPress REST API date of the plugin's auto-created registration page, combined with a single-MD5 oracle (`md5(key|level)`) that the public registration form prints as `swpm_level_hash` and a non-constant-time `!=` comparison in `SwpmFrontRegistration::register_front_end()` as the sole authorization gate on which membership level a visitor may register into; `SwpmUtils::get_free_level()` then honors an attacker-posted `level_identifier=md5(level)` regardless of the configured free-membership setting, and `prepare_and_create_wp_user_front_end()` creates the WordPress account with whatever role the level is configured to grant (only the `administrator` role is refused). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers, after an offline brute-force recovery of the install-time secret against the public MD5 oracle, to forge a valid `swpm_level_hash` for any configured membership level and self-register into that level, elevating their newly created WordPress account to the level's assigned role — e. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete editor role.

The WP Review Slider plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Read in versions up to, and including, 15.5 via the wprp_twitter_savetweet and wpfb_avatar_tolocal AJAX actions. This is due to the handlers only verifying a WordPress nonce without any current_user_can() capability check and accepting an attacker-supplied local filesystem path in the 'tw_img' parameter, which is later passed directly to PHP's copy() to write byte-identical data into a publicly accessible uploads directory under an attacker-chosen name. The nonce action 'randomnoncestring' is shared with the same vendor's companion plugin (WP Google Review Slider), which emits it to every visitor of every front-end page, making it obtainable by any logged-in user including Subscribers whenever that companion plugin is active. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to read arbitrary files on the affected site's server, including sensitive files such as wp-config.

The LA-Studio Element Kit for Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'actions[].data.settings.triggers.scrolling_to_selector' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The elementor_ajax nonce required to reach the handler is printed in elementorCommonConfig on every wp-admin page, making it trivially obtainable by any logged-in Subscriber via /wp-admin/profile.php; although Elementor's attribute escaping is applied at render time, the stored selector value is subsequently passed to jQuery() by the popup frontend script, which re-parses strings beginning with '<' as HTML, bypassing the escaping.

The PDF Invoice for WooCommerce + Drag and Drop Template Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 7.2.0 via deserialization of untrusted input . This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject a PHP Object. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable software, which means this vulnerability has no impact unless another plugin or theme containing a POP chain is installed on the site. If a POP chain is present via an additional plugin or theme installed on the target system, it may allow the attacker to perform actions like delete arbitrary files, retrieve sensitive data, or execute code depending on the POP chain present. The incomplete remediation in version 7.2.0 applied escape_pdf_note() only to the customer_note path; the billing address path at woocommerce/shortcodes.php:975–978 remains unpatched, and exploitation requires guest checkout to be enabled along with a payment method that transitions orders to on-hold status (such as the stock WooCommerce Direct Bank Transfer option).

A vulnerability was identified in SourceCodester Online Food Ordering System 1.0. This impacts an unknown function of the file food-search.php of the component Food Search. The manipulation of the argument Search leads to cross site scripting. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used.

A security flaw has been discovered in SourceCodester Online Food Ordering System 1.0. Affected is the function move_uploaded_file of the file /admin/add_food.php of the component File Upload Handler. The manipulation of the argument image/new_image/update_image results in unrestricted upload. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks.

A weakness has been identified in SourceCodester Syllabus-Aligned Learning Management & Examination System 1.0. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file approve_enrollment.php. This manipulation causes open redirect. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks.

SiYuan from 3.6.2 before 3.8.10 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows admin token holders to read files outside the workspace because the globalCopyFiles and workspaceCopyFiles denylist omits /home, /mnt, /media, and /snap. Attackers can copy other users' SSH authorized_keys, Docker and AWS configs, or mounted files into the workspace and retrieve them via the getFile API.

Traefik before 2.11.62, 3.x before 3.7.18, and 3.8.0-rc.1 contain an authentication bypass in the ForwardAuth middleware because connection isolation for NTLM and Negotiate credentials checks only the Authorization header, not Proxy-Authorization. Unauthenticated attackers can send such credentials in Proxy-Authorization to reuse a shared authentication-server connection already authenticated by another user, receive that user's identity via authResponseHeaders, and access backends as that user.

Traefik 3.1.0 before 3.7.18 and 3.8.0-rc.1 contain a memory exhaustion vulnerability in the Compress middleware, which creates zstd encoders with library default options that retain about 18 MiB of state per response until it is fully written. Unauthenticated remote attackers can open many concurrent requests and read responses slowly to exhaust memory and crash Traefik.

Traefik 3.7.15 before 3.7.18 and 3.8.0-rc.1 before 3.8.0-rc.2 contains a client certificate authentication bypass in the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider because, on hosts shared by multiple Ingresses using auth-tls-secret, Ssl-Client-* headers are built per Ingress while the TLS handshake uses the first Ingress's settings. Unauthenticated remote attackers can obtain Ssl-Client-Verify: SUCCESS with a client-chosen subject and issuer for an unverified certificate, or inject Ssl-Client-* headers directly, presenting forged identities to backends that trust the proxy.

Traefik before 2.11.62, 3.x before 3.7.18, and 3.8.0-rc.1 contain an authorization bypass because the sanitizePath entry point option leaves dot-segments carrying path parameters, such as /..;x/, unresolved when matching routers and applying middlewares. Unauthenticated attackers can send requests like /public/..;x/admin to a parameter-stripping backend shared with a protected router, bypassing authentication or authorization middlewares to reach protected resources.

Traefik before 2.11.62, 3.x before 3.7.18, and 3.8.0-rc.1 before 3.8.0-rc.2 contain a denial of service vulnerability in the BasicAuth middleware, which does not limit password length before MD5-crypt ($apr1$, $1$) hashing. Unauthenticated attackers can send passwords up to the entry point maxHeaderBytes limit (1 MiB by default), consuming excessive CPU per request and degrading availability.

OpenWrt LuCI luci-app-unbound through 26.288.56989~75a306d contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because the Unbound Configure page inserts the dhcp.odhcpd.leasetrigger value into a warning notification without escaping. Users with delegated network configuration access can store an HTML event handler in that option through the permitted uci RPC, which executes in an administrator's browser session when the page renders.

Budibase Server from 3.39.18 before 4.0.0 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to erase MongoDB query filters by supplying __proto__ as a dynamic JSON key in PUBLIC queries. Attackers can send a single request to the query execution endpoint, reducing the filter to {} to read, update, or delete every document in the collection.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated same-organization users to invoke OAuth2 authorization on data sources they cannot configure. Attackers can send POST requests to /api/data-sources/:id/authorize_oauth2 to bind attacker-controlled OAuth credentials or overwrite token state for foreign data sources.

LaraDashboard before 1.5.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in module.json providers and composer.json psr-4 namespace parsing that derives destination folder names without excluding traversal characters. Attackers with module.create permission can upload a crafted module ZIP to write PHP files into the public directory, achieving unauthenticated remote code execution.

Coder before 2.29.27, 2.30.0 before 2.34.19, 2.35.0 before 2.37.11, 2.38.0 before 2.38.7, and 2.39.0 before 2.39.1 returns database connection errors containing a temporary AWS IAM database password in API key middleware responses. During database connection failures, unauthenticated attackers can send a well-formed but invalid API key to obtain the password and access the PostgreSQL database for 15 minutes.

web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6 allow CPU exhaustion because, on PHP without GMP, AbstractECDH falls back to pure PHP curve code that converts unbounded ECDH-ES epk x and y coordinates to big integers before any length check. Unauthenticated attackers who know only the recipient key's curve can send small JWEs with oversized epk coordinates, keeping workers busy for seconds to minutes per token.

web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.13, 4.0.0 before 4.0.9, 4.1.0 before 4.1.11, and 4.2.0 before 4.2.6 does not check oct key length in the AESKW, AESGCMKW, and experimental AESCTR and chacha20-poly1305 key encryption algorithms, so OpenSSL zero-pads short or empty keys. When an application uses an empty key, anyone can unwrap content encryption keys under the all-zero key to read issued tokens and forge accepted ones.

web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6 parse JSON General serialized JWS tokens in quadratic time because JSONGeneralSerializer::unserialize() adds each signature via JWS::addSignature(), which clones the token. Unauthenticated remote attackers can send large tokens holding thousands of empty signatures to exhaust CPU and occupy PHP workers without any valid key or token.

The WebP Express plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authorization Bypass via Malformed Bcrypt Salt in all versions up to, and including, 0.25.15. This is due to insufficient validation of the attacker-supplied `salt` POST parameter in the `runAccessChecks()` function, which passes the unvalidated salt directly to PHP's `crypt()` — causing it to return an empty string when the salt contains characters outside the valid bcrypt alphabet `[./0-9A-Za-z]` — and then loosely compares the resulting empty string against the attacker-controlled `api-key-crypted` POST parameter using `==`, allowing an empty submission to match and satisfy the check. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to bypass the web service API-key authentication check and upload arbitrary image files to the cloud-conversion endpoint, where they persist at a predictable, publicly reachable path under `wp-content/webp-express/webp-images/wpc/`. The 'Require api-key to be crypted in transfer?' whitelist setting does not mitigate this bypass, as it only gates the plaintext API-key comparison branch and has no effect on the crypted-key branch containing the vulnerable logic.

A security vulnerability has been detected in Max Foundry Media Library Folders Plugin up to 8.4.3 on WordPress. Affected by this issue is the function mlfp_toggle_file_access of the file media-library-plus.php of the component Block Direct Access. Such manipulation of the argument file_id leads to missing authorization. The attack can be executed remotely. Upgrading to version 8.4.4 can resolve this issue. You should upgrade the affected component.

It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used.

A vulnerability was determined in projectworlds Online Jewellery Shopping System 1.0. A vulnerability was identified in itsourcecode Event Management System 1.0. The impacted element is an unknown function of the file view_event.php. Such manipulation of the argument ID leads to sql injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used.

The Apache Airflow TaskFlow decorators @task.bash, @task.sql, @task.analytics, @task.kubernetes_cmd and the common.ai decorators (@task.llm, @task.agent, @task.llm_sql, @task.llm_branch, @task.llm_file_analysis, @task.llm_schema_compare) rendered Jinja templates a second time after the task runner had already rendered them, so any value copied into env, op_args, op_kwargs or the returned prompt, command or SQL was evaluated as a template on the worker. An attacker who can only trigger a Dag run (for example a user with trigger permission supplying run conf), or who controls text that a Dag passes into one of these decorators as an argument or prompt (for example a ticket or a downloaded document), could run arbitrary commands on the worker and read connection passwords and Variables, in any deployment that uses an affected decorator in a Dag that passes such input through env, parameters or prompt. Users are recommended to upgrade apache-airflow-providers-standard to 1.22.0, apache-airflow-providers-cncf-kubernetes to 11.0.0, apache-airflow-providers-common-sql to 3.0.0 and apache-airflow-providers-common-ai to 1.2.0 or later.

Docker Sandboxes re-resolves saved mount paths when replacing a sandbox container during kit changes or restarting a sandbox. An attacker able to replace a source ancestor in a shared writable workspace with a symlink can redirect another sandbox's mount to a different host directory, exposing its contents and permitting modification through read-write mounts. The destination must remain accessible to the daemon and allowed by policy where enforced. Saved-mount replay during kit replacement was introduced in version 0.35.0; ordinary restart replay was added in version 0.45.0. This saved-mount replay issue is fixed in version 0.54.0.

A flaw was found in Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security (ACS). An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit a vulnerability in the login interface's OAuth callback endpoint by crafting a malicious URL. This URL, containing unvalidated `error` and `error_uri` parameters, allows the attacker to display arbitrary error messages, leading to content spoofing. Furthermore, the attacker can redirect victims to malicious domains, effectively performing an open redirect under the guise of the trusted application's user interface.

An **uncontrolled memory allocation** flaw has been found in the smbd_smb2_ioctl_pipe_write_done() function in source3/smbd/smb2_ioctl_named_pipe.c of the SMB2 named-pipe ioctl handling in the samba package. The file server reserves memory for a named-pipe response using a size chosen by the client. It does not keep that size within the maximum the client and the server have already agreed. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can open a named pipe can request a very large response. The file server reserves that memory before it reads the pipe and holds it until the request ends. Repeating this on more connections can exhaust memory and keep the file service unavailable while those requests continue.

In LXD before 5.21.0 and 6.10.0, an OS command injection vulnerability allows an authenticated client restricted to a single project to execute arbitrary code as root on the host.

 The raw.dnsmasq bridge network configuration key is not restricted to server administrators and is copied verbatim into the dnsmasq configuration file, so a user whose project keeps the default features.networks=false can have a bridge network created in the default project with an injected dhcp-script directive. This allows an attacker to make the host dnsmasq execute attacker-chosen code as root on a DHCP lease event and fully compromise the host.

Configuration injection in virtual machine disk device handling in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with VM creation permissions in a restricted project to bypass low-level VM restrictions and control the root QEMU process via quotes and line breaks in a disk device's guest path.

Improper output encoding in Prometheus metrics exposition in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows a user controlling a virtual machine to forge host metric labels and break metrics scraping via unescaped guest-controlled filesystem mountpoints and network interface names.

Path traversal in container device path resolution and VM disk format detection in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with project access, including an unprivileged local user through lxd-user, to read and modify arbitrary host files or Ceph RBD images and gain root privileges on the host via crafted device paths or QCOW2 backing file references.

Exposure of sensitive information in API responses, exports, and host-side artifacts in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated lower-privileged user or a local host user to read credentials, private keys, and other projects' metadata and inject arguments into Ceph administration commands via unfiltered endpoints, exported configurations, log files, process command lines, and unvalidated bucket parameters.

Exposure of resource to wrong sphere in optimized ZFS backup imports in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access to mount an attacker-controlled filesystem over arbitrary host paths and execute code as root on the host via importing a filesystem ZFS stream declared as a block volume.
